Kǒngzǐ said,
"Respect, reverence, loyalty, and trustworthiness
can preserve oneself.
Respect avoids being scorned by the masses,
reverence makes people love you,
loyalty makes people support you,
and trustworthiness makes people rely on you.
If a person is loved,
if a person gives,
if a person is relied upon,
then he will surely avoid calamity.
He can govern a state,
how much more so himself!"
*Shuō Yuàn · Zá Yán* Zǐ Lù was about to depart and
took leave of Zhòng Ní. He said:
"Shall I give you a carriage?
Or some words?"
Zǐ Lù said:
"Please give me words."
Zhòng Ní said:
"Without strength, one cannot go far;
without toil, there is no achievement;
without loyalty, there are no relatives;
without trustworthiness, there is no return;
without respect, there is no propriety.
Be careful of these five,
and you can last for a long time."
*Shuō Yuàn · Zá Yán* Kǒngzǐ said:
"The nature of ordinary people is that
with excess, they become extravagant;
with insufficiency, they become frugal;
without prohibitions, they become licentious;
without limits, they lose their way;
indulging desires leads to ruin.
Have measure in food and drink,
"Clothing should have its limits;
palaces should have their standards;
possessions should have their numbers;
vehicles and utensils should have their boundaries—
these are to prevent the source of disorder."
Therefore, standards of measurement must not be unclear,
and good desires must not be ignored.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"The gentleman speaks all day without neglecting his own worries,
acts all day without neglecting his own troubles—
only the wise possess this.
Therefore, fear and apprehension are the means to eliminate troubles,
and respect and reverence are the means to overcome difficulties.
One can spend a lifetime building it up,
but ruin it with a single word;
how can one not be careful!"
Yán Yuān asked Zhòngní:
"What is the conduct of an accomplished person like?"
The Master said:
"The conduct of an accomplished person
understands the principles of emotions and nature,
is versed in the changes of things,
knows the reasons for the hidden and the manifest,
and perceives the origins of wandering qi.
If one is like this,
then one can be called an accomplished person.
Having understood the Way of Heaven,
one conducts oneself with benevolence and righteousness,
Cultivate oneself with propriety and music.
For benevolence, righteousness, propriety, and music
are the practices of a complete person.
Exhausting the mysteries and understanding transformations
is the pinnacle of virtue."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Excessive wealth harms virtue,
and when exhausted, it leads to a lack of propriety."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"If you want others to trust you,
then speak cautiously and act sincerely.
If you act sincerely, then you will be employed for a long time.
If you are employed for a long time, then your deeds will become clear and obvious.
When your deeds are clear and obvious, there is no eye that does not see them,
and no ear that does not hear them.
How can they be false!"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Only the junzi (gentleman) is capable of valuing his words
and valuing his countenance.
Can a xiaoren (petty person) do this?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"The xiaoren use slander and criticism as argument,
pressing and urgency as wisdom,
and disrespect as courage."
Six Arts, Four Above
Zhòngní
was a person from Lǔ.
When he was born, he did not know the origin of the Yì (Changes).
I once divined his fate,
and obtained the hexagram *Lǚ* (旅, The Wanderer).
I sought further explanation from Shāng Qú shì. He said,
"You possess the wisdom of a sage but lack a position."
Kǒngzǐ wept and said,
"It is Heaven! It is fate!
The phoenix does not appear,
and the Yellow River produces no chart.
Alas!
It is the decree of Heaven!"
After finishing this lament, he ceased his ambition,
stopped reading the *Lǐ* (禮, Rites),
and halted his historical editing.
At fifty, he mastered the *Yì* (易, Book of Changes),
and wrote the *Shí Yì* (十翼, Ten Wings),
clarifying it,
clarifying the subtle teachings of the *Yì*.
He said:
"Working all day long,
I contemplate the ancient sages,
and take Yí (頤, Nourishment) as my teacher, and follow the laws of Jī Chāng and Fǎ Dàn."
He wrote *Jiǔ Wèn* (九問, Nine Questions), *Shí È* (十惡, Ten Evils),
*Qī Zhèng* (七正, Seven Correctives), *Bā Tàn* (八歎, Eight Sighs),
the Upper and Lower Appended Statements,
the Great Way, the Great Numbers,
the Great Laws, and the Great Meanings.
Within the *Yì* book is a question for communicating with the sacred;
the enlightened consider it to be the work of sages and worthies.
Confucius said:
"I observe them and say that,
the benevolent see it as the pattern of benevolence, the subtleties of benevolence,
the wise see it as the questions of wisdom, the subtleties of wisdom,
and the sage sees it as the pattern of communication with the divine.
The benevolent see it and practice benevolence,
the wise see it and practice wisdom.
They follow benevolence and wisdom."
*Zhōu Yì Qián Záo Dù*. Confucius said:
"The *Yì* is,
ease,
change,
and constancy.
It governs the three achievements and virtues,
and embraces the subtle and profound aspects of the Way.
The *Yì*
speaks of its virtue,
communicates feelings without a gate,
and conceals spirit without an interior.
Its brightness pervades in all four directions,
and through interaction, principles are established.
Heaven and Earth shine brightly,
the sun, moon, and stars are arranged,
the eight trigrams are placed in their order,
the musical scales and calendar are harmonized,
the five planets follow their orbits,
and the four seasons bring harmonious budding and fruition.
The four rivers communicate feelings,
Leisurely and trustworthy in purity,
rooted amidst the floating stream,
the vital energy further substantiates each other,
emptiness evokes emotion,
purity and stillness illuminate wisdom,
moving objects to bring forth brilliance,
utmost sincerity, focused and secret,
not vexed, not yielding,
detached, yet not lost.
This is its ease.
Changeability is,
its vital energy.
Heaven and earth, if unchanging,
cannot circulate their energies.
The Five Elements alternately end and begin,
the Four Seasons replace and abolish each other.
Ruler and ministers take their images,
changing their deportment to harmonize with each other,
those who can dissipate will rest,
those who are necessarily single-minded will fail.
Ruler and ministers, if unchanging,
cannot form a dynasty.
Zhòu acted with cruelty,
heaven and earth rebelled.
King Wén employed Lǚ,
and a nine-tailed fox was seen.
Husband and wife, if unchanging,
cannot form a family.
Dájǐ indulged in favoritism,
and Yīn was destroyed because of it.
Dà Rèn followed the proper seasons,
and the dynasty enjoyed the country for seven hundred years.
This is the aspect of change.
What is unchanging
is its position.
Heaven is above,
earth is below,
the ruler faces south,
the ministers face north,
the father sits, the son prostrates.
This is the aspect of what does not change.
Therefore, change is
the way of Heaven and Earth.
The virtue of Qián and Kūn
is the treasure of all things.
How supreme is the *Yì*,
using unity as the basis for all principles."
Confucius said:
"In the time of remote antiquity,
the people were undifferentiated,
all things were indistinguishable,
and there were no benefits from clothing, food, or utensils.
Thereupon, Fúxī looked up to observe the images in the heavens,
looked down to observe the patterns on the earth,
and observed the suitability of all things in between.
He then created the eight trigrams,
To communicate the virtues of the spirits,
and to categorize the emotions of all things.
Therefore, the *Yì* [Book of Changes]
is that by which Heaven and Earth are continued,
the principles of human relationships are ordered, and the Way of the King is clarified.
Therefore, the eight trigrams are established,
the five *qì* are set in place,
and the five constant virtues are enacted by them.
It imitates the patterns of *Qián* (Heaven) and *Kūn* (Earth),
accords with *yīn* and *yáng*,
to rectify the righteousness of ruler and subject, father and son, husband and wife.
It measures the times and regulates what is appropriate,
and makes nets and snares
for hunting and fishing,
to provide for the people's needs.
Thereupon, the people are well-governed,
the ruler and parents are honored,
ministers and sons are obedient,
all living beings live in harmony,
and each finds peace in its own nature.
This is the use of the eight trigrams.
When *Fúxī* shì ruled the world,
he first created the eight trigrams,
and knotted cords to make nets and snares,
for hunting and fishing.
This was taken from the *Lí* trigram.
The substance is without embellishment;
speaking with respect to Heaven,
This is the meaning of change in the *Yì*.
The transformations of the eight trigrams
are images that resonate with people.
Wén Wáng, according to the suitability of human nature and emotions,
created regulations for them."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"The *Yì* begins with the Supreme Ultimate (*Tàijí*).
The Supreme Ultimate divides and becomes two,
thus giving birth to Heaven and Earth.
Heaven and Earth have the seasons of spring, autumn, winter, and summer,
thus giving birth to the four seasons.
Each of the four seasons has divisions of yin and yang, firmness and gentleness,
thus giving birth to the eight trigrams.
When the eight trigrams are arranged,
the Way of Heaven and Earth is established,
and the images of thunder, wind, water, fire, mountain, and marsh are determined.
Their distribution and application in affairs is such that
*zhèn* generates things in the east,
its position is in the second month;
*xùn* scatters them in the southeast,
its position is in the fourth month;
*lí* causes them to grow in the south,
its position is in the fifth month;
*kūn* nourishes them in the southwest,
its position is in the sixth month;
*duì* gathers them in the west,
its position is in the eighth month;
*qián* controls them in the northwest,
Lí is located in the tenth month;
Kǎn is hidden in the north,
located in the eleventh month;
Gèn finishes and begins in the northeast,
located in the twelfth month.
When the qi of the eight trigrams ends,
then the distinctions of the four cardinal directions and four corners are clear,
the ways of birth, growth, gathering, and storage are complete,
the substance of yin and yang is settled,
the virtue of spiritual enlightenment is communicated,
and the myriad things are each completed according to their kind.
All are encompassed by the *Yì*.
How perfect!
The virtue of the *Yì*."
*Zhōu Yì Qián Záo Dù*. Kǒngzǐ said:
"The year has three hundred and sixty days, and the heavenly qi cycles completely.
The eight trigrams each govern for forty-five days,
thus completing the year.
Therefore, Gèn gradually advances in the first month,
Xùn gradually advances in the third month,
Kūn gradually advances in the seventh month,
Qián gradually advances in the ninth month,
and each month is according to what is said in the trigram.
Qián is
Heaven,
ending and becoming the beginning of all things;
the north
is where all things begin,
Therefore, the position of Qián is in the tenth month.
Gèn means,
that which stops things.
Therefore, it is at the end of the four seasons,
its position is in the twelfth month;
Xùn means,
the Yin begins to follow the Yang,
the Yang begins to grow strong in the southeast,
therefore its position is in the fourth month.
Kūn means,
the way of the Earth,
its form is established in the sixth month,
the four cardinal directions are correctly ordered,
the warp and weft are balanced,
and the sequence of degrees is complete."
Confucius said:
"Qián and Kūn are,
the masters of Yin and Yang.
Yang begins in Hài,
takes shape in Chǒu,
the position of Qián is in the northwest,
Yang's ancestor subtly relies on the beginning.
Yin begins in Sì,
takes shape in Wèi,
relying on correctness to establish its position,
therefore the position of Kūn is in the southwest,
the correctness of Yin.
The way of the ruler initiates,
The way of a minister is ultimately to be upright,
therefore the position of Qián 乾 is in hài 亥,
and the position of Kūn 坤 is in wèi 未.
This is to clarify the duties of yin and yang
and establish the positions of ruler and minister."
Confucius said:
"Once the order of the eight trigrams is established,
then the five elements transform into shapes.
Therefore, when a person is born, they correspond to the structure of the eight trigrams,
and receive the five elements to become the five constant virtues,
which are benevolence, righteousness, propriety, wisdom, and faithfulness.
All things initially emerge from Zhèn 震, Zhèn,
is the trigram of the east.
The yang qi begins to generate,
receiving the way of form,
therefore the east is associated with benevolence.
They are completed in Lí 離, Lí,
is the trigram of the south.
Yang obtains its proper position above,
yin obtains its proper position below,
the image of superior and inferior is established,
which is the order of propriety,
therefore the south is associated with propriety.
They enter into Duì 兌, Duì,
is the trigram of the west.
Yin takes charge and all things obtain what is suitable,
which is the principle of righteousness,
therefore the west is associated with righteousness.
Gradually [becoming] like Kan; Kan,
is the hexagram of the north,
the yin energy is strong in form,
the yin and yang energies are contained and closed,
[it is] the category of trustworthiness,
therefore the north is trustworthiness.
Now, the meanings of the four directions
are all governed by the center,
therefore Qian, Kun, Gen, Xun,
are located in the four corners,
the center is that by which the four directions are governed,
[it is] the decision of wisdom,
therefore the center is wisdom.
Therefore the Way arises from benevolence,
is established in ritual,
is ordered by righteousness,
is settled in trustworthiness,
is completed in wisdom.
These five,
are the divisions of morality,
and the boundary between heaven and man.
The sages therefore understand the will of heaven,
regulate human relationships, and illuminate the ultimate Way."
"Zhou Yi Qian Zao Du." Confucius said:
"Yang is three, yin is four,
this is the correctness of their positions,
therefore the Changes hexagrams are sixty-four,
divided into upper and lower,
This symbolizes Yīn and Yáng.
The way of Yáng is unifying and odd,
therefore the upper section has thirty chapters,
to symbolize Yáng.
The way of Yīn is impure and even,
therefore the lower section has thirty-four chapters,
to model Yīn.
Qián and Kūn
are the root of Yīn and Yáng,
the ancestors of all things.
Beginning the upper section with them
is to honor them.
Lí is the sun,
Kǎn is the moon,
the way of the sun and moon
is the warp and weft of Yīn and Yáng,
therefore they begin and end all things;
thus Kǎn and Lí are used as the conclusion.
Xián and Héng
are the beginning of male and female,
the way of husband and wife.
The flourishing of humanity
must come from husband and wife,
therefore they serve the ancestors,
and become masters of Heaven and Earth.
Thus, beginning the lower section with them
is to value them.
Jì Jì and Wèi Jì being the final chapters
Therefore, one should clearly be cautious and preserve the way of the King."
*Jīng* Family's *Classic of Changes Commentary*, Volume 2. Kǒngzǐ said:
"Yang is three, Yin is four,
these are the correct positions.
Three
is the number of the East.
The East is where the sun rises,
also, a circle has a diameter of one and opens into three.
Four
is the number of the West.
The West is where the sun sets,
also, a square
with a diameter of one takes up four.
This speaks of the way of the sun and moon completing the sky.
Therefore, the hexagrams of the *Classic of Changes* are sixty-four,
divided into upper and lower,
symbolizing Yin and Yang.
The numbers of odd and even
are taken from *Qián* and *Kūn*.
*Qián* and *Kūn*
are the root of Yin and Yang.
*Kǎn* and *Lí*
are the nature and life of Yin and Yang.
Divide into four operations to complete the *Classic of Changes*,
eighteen transformations to complete a hexagram.
Once the hexagram image is determined,
good and bad fortune are clear,
gain and loss descend,
The five elements are divided.
When the four symbols (sì xiàng) are in harmony, it is auspicious;
when they are reversed, it is inauspicious.
Therefore, it is said that fortune, misfortune, regret, and disgrace arise from movement.
It is also said that one understands gain and loss through the four seasons.
The mechanism of fate unfolds and spreads;
its Qi transforms and changes.
The one in charge should also act appropriately,
thus following Heaven's way
and adapting to the times.
Remain secure without forgetting potential ruin,
in order to comply with the principles of nature and destiny,
and thoroughly understand the source of the yarrow stalks and tortoise shell (divination).
Redoubling three to become six (referring to the hexagrams),
the task will be completed.
Dividing the images of Heaven and Earth, Qián (乾) and Kūn (坤),
and adding Jiǎ (甲), Yǐ (乙), Rén (壬), and Guǐ (癸);
the images of Zhèn (震) and Xùn (巽) are paired with Gēng (庚) and Xīn (辛);
the images of Kǎn (坎) and Lí (離) are paired with Wù (戊) and Jǐ (己);
the images of Gèn (艮) and Duì (兌) are paired with Bǐng (丙) and Dīng (丁).
The eight trigrams divide into yin and yang, six positions, and five elements,
with light penetrating in all four directions,
transformation and change establishing the rules.
If Heaven and Earth did not transform and change,
they could not communicate Qi.
The five elements alternate to their end,
the four seasons replace each other.
Change and movement never cease,
Circulating through the six voids,
rising and falling without constancy,
the hard and soft interchange,
cannot be taken as fixed principles.
Only adapt to change,
good and bad fortune are both arranged in their positions,
advancement and retreat are clear regarding the crucial points,
the changes of the *Yì* are in the six lines,
and cannot be relied upon for divination at any given time."
Confucius said:
" *Tài*
is when Heaven and Earth communicate,
*yīn* and *yáng* are in action,
nurturing the myriad things;
*Fǒu* is when
Heaven and Earth do not communicate,
*yīn* and *yáng* are not in action,
and the growth of the myriad things stops.
The Upper Canon symbolizes *yáng*,
therefore *Qián* is taken as the beginning,
and *Kūn* as the next,
first *Tài* and then *Fǒu*.
*Sǔn* is when *yīn* is in action,
the marsh diminishes the mountain, and the myriad things diminish,
the lower diminish to serve the upper;
*Yì* is when *yáng* is in action,
and thunder and wind benefit the myriad things,
the upper diminish themselves to benefit the lower.
The Lower Canon takes Yin as its model,
therefore it begins with Xián (咸),
and follows with Héng (恒).
First decrease and then increase,
each following its kind."
*Zhōu Yì Qián Záo Dù* Confucius said:
"Shēng (升)
is the hexagram of the twelfth month.
The Yang Qi rises upward,
the Yin Qi desires to receive it,
and all things begin to advance.
It is like King Wén's (文王) cultivation of accumulated virtue,
and the grand opening of his foundation,
beginning on the path of great peace.
At this time,
neighboring states are transformed,
and the people of Qí (岐) are harmonious and well-disposed.
Therefore, the sixth in the fourth place receives favor and inherits good fortune,
and the ninth in the third place can occupy the royal position,
and make offerings at Mount Qí (岐山),
as a way of repaying virtue.
Manifesting Yin to reveal the transformation of Yang,
the people and ministers follow virtue,
therefore it is said that there is no blame."
*Zhōu Yì Qián Záo Dù* Confucius said:
"The sixth in the second place of Yì (益),
perhaps bestows it with ten pairs of tortoise shells,
and cannot be opposed.
*Yǒng zhēn jí*,
*wáng yòng xiǎng yú dì*. *Jí*,
the *yì* (increase)
is the hexagram of the first month.
The *tiān qì* (heavenly energy) descends and bestows,
all things benefit.
It speaks of the king's method of emulating Heaven and Earth,
implementing governance and teachings,
and the world being covered by the virtue of *yáng*,
receiving the king's transformative influence,
like beautiful treasure,
none can disobey or harm.
Persistently upholding this correct path,
all receive auspicious transformation,
virtue extends to the four seas,
able to continue the Way of Heaven.
"The king uses sacrifice to the Emperor"
speaks of sacrificing to Heaven.
The suburban sacrifices of the Three Kings
all used the Xia calendar.
The heavenly energy accumulates in small increments to form a manifestation;
three manifestations form a complete entity.
Only then is it known that at this time,
Heaven and Earth interact,
all things communicate.
Therefore, the hexagrams of *Tài* (Peace) and *Yì* (Increase)
are all based on the Xia calendar.
This is the correctness of the four seasons,
an unchanging Way.
Therefore, the suburban sacrifices of the Three Kings
all used the Xia calendar,
in order to accord with the four seasons
and emulate the Way of Heaven and Earth."
*Zhōu Yì Qián Záo Dù* (Apochryphal Commentary on the Book of Changes) Confucius said:
"In the *Suí* hexagram, line six at the top,
is restrained and bound,
and then follows from the rope.
The king uses it to make offerings on Mount Xī.
*Suí* is the hexagram of the second month.
The virtue of *Suí* is put into practice,
[when] the fence is broken and difficult to untie,
all things follow the yang and emerge.
Therefore, line six at the top desires that nine in the fifth place restrain and bind it,
and maintain it,
illustrating being influenced by the transformation of yang, and the yin following and complying.
It is like King Wén's exaltation of supreme virtue,
manifesting the beauty of equilibrium and harmony,
restraining the people with ritual,
and binding the people with righteousness.
At this time,
where benevolence and grace are bestowed,
none do not follow and comply.
All delight in his virtue,
and obtain a king who employs the Way.
Therefore, it is said that the king uses it to make offerings on Mount Xī."
Confucius said:
"When *yáng* diminishes, *yīn* speaks.
When *yīn* diminishes, *yáng* speaks of stripping away.
This is the origin of all things.
To sever, control, eliminate harm,
and make the preservation of things one's task
is what is meant by *jué* (決, Resoluteness).
When it is the time of the third month,
*yáng* is flourishing and growing, *yīn* dwindling and ceasing,
and the *qì* of *yīn*
all things are completely born,
without exception, receiving transformation.
It is like a king who exalts supreme virtue,
reverently receiving Heaven's mandate,
decisively eliminating petty people,
in order to bring peace to the common people;
therefore it is called *jué*.
The harm done by *yīn* becomes an action;
therefore, to strip away becomes the action of stripping.
When it is the time of the ninth month,
the *yáng qì* declines and diminishes,
but *yīn* ultimately cannot completely overcome *yáng*;
petty people cannot decisively eliminate gentlemen.
This is called *bō* (剝, Stripping Away),
meaning unease and nothing more.
Therefore, regarding the ninth and fifth lines, it speaks of *jué*;
petty people strip it away.
Regarding the sixth and fifth lines, it speaks of flourishing and killing all things;
all strip off and fall away.
It is like the way of the superior man declining,
and the way of the petty man flourishing,
aggressive actions arising,
and the way of safety being abandoned.
The *yīn* line pierces through like a string of fish, wanting to receive the superior man."
*Zhōu Yì Qián Záo Dù*. Kǒngzǐ said:
"The *Yì* has six positions and three powers,
which are the boundaries of the ways of Heaven, Earth, and Man.
The ways of the three powers
are Heaven, Earth, and Man.
Heaven has *yīn* and *yáng*,
Earth has yielding and firm,
Man has benevolence and righteousness.
Emulating these three,
therefore the six positions are produced.
The changes of the six positions:
the *yáng* lines
are governed by Heaven,
the *yīn* lines
are connected to Earth.
Heaven moves and bestows, which is called benevolence;
Earth is still and manages, which is called righteousness.
When benevolence is completed, it rises upwards;
when righteousness is completed, it descends downwards.
That which is above solely governs,
that which is below obediently follows.
When correctness takes form in man,
then moral principles are established and hierarchy is determined.
This is the dividing line between the Way of Heaven and Earth and the Way of Man.
The Qi of Heaven and Earth
must have a beginning and an end.
The arrangement of the six positions
all follows the order of above and below.
Therefore, the *Yì* begins with One,
divides into Two,
connects into Three,
*[illegible]* into Four,
flourishes into Five,
and ends with Above.
The initial position is *yuán shì* (元士, primary scholar),
the second is *dàfū* (大夫, grand master),
the third is *sāngōng* (三公, the three dukes/ministers),
the fourth is *zhūhóu* (諸侯, feudal lords),
the fifth is *tiānzǐ* (天子, the Son of Heaven),
and the upper position is the ancestral temple (*zōngmiào* 宗廟).
All these six are
how Yin and Yang advance and retreat,
how ruler and subject ascend and descend,
and how the myriad people take them as models.
Therefore, Yin and Yang have waxing and waning,
and the Way of Man has gain and loss.
The sage observes these phenomena,
follows their changes,
and establishes hexagrams accordingly.
When something is flourishing, it presages good fortune;
when it is about to decline, it foreshadows misfortune.
If Yin and Yang are not correct,
it is all due to a loss of position,
and when the response is substantial and possessed,
it is all a loss of righteousness.
Even if goodness is slight,
it will inevitably show auspicious signs;
Even if evil is minute,
there will certainly be regret and distress.
Therefore, to fully understand the changes of heaven and earth,
and to exhaust the true nature of all things,
is the task of an enlightened ruler.
Qiū explained it, saying:
"Establish images to fully express meaning,
set up the guà to fully express true and false intentions,
attach explanations to them to fully express their words."
*Zhōu Yì Qián Záo Dù* Confucius said:
"When the six positions of the *Yì* are correct,
the standards of the ruler will be revealed."
*Zhōu Yì Qián Záo Dù* Confucius said:
"The *Yì* has five titles for a ruler:
Dì is
a title of Heaven;
Wáng is
a title of excellent conduct;
Tiānzǐ is
a title of nobility;
Dàjūn is
different in its actions from those above;
A dà rén is one whose
sage-like intelligence and virtuous character are complete.
They alter writing to make a name,
and inscribe virtue to distinguish conduct.
A wáng is
the one to whom all under Heaven turn and submit.
The *Yì* says:
“Being in the midst of the army
brings good fortune without blame;
the king bestows commands three times.”
*Shī* means the masses.
This speaks of possessing flourishing virtue,
acting with moderation and harmony,
and according with the hearts of the people.

The way to maintain fullness
is to suppress and diminish it.
This is the virtue of humility in practice.
Those who follow it will be blessed;
those who oppose it will meet with misfortune.
After the Five Emperors passed away,
and the Three Kings declined,
among those who could practice the virtue of humility,
was it not only Zhōu Gōng?
He was the son of Wén Wáng,
the younger brother of Wǔ Wáng,
the uncle of Chéng Wáng,
For seven years, he falsely held the esteemed position of the Son of Heaven.
Ten people presented gifts to him, acknowledging him as their teacher.
Thirteen people returned gifts, regarding him as their friend.
Of the scholars from poor alleys and humble dwellings,
forty-nine were the first to be received by him.
One hundred people were promptly promoted for their goodness.
One thousand people attended court.
He had five remonstrating ministers.
He had five assisting ministers.
He had six corrective ministers.
One hundred men of the same surname carried weapons until they were enfeoffed as lords.
One hundred men of the same surname.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"If the Duke of Zhōu were to reward the world,
he would consider those of the same clan as many,
and those of a different clan as few."
Therefore, if one's virtue and conduct are broad and tolerant,
guarding them with respectfulness brings honor.
If one's territory is vast and extensive,
guarding it with frugality brings peace.
If one's position is high and one's emolument is great,
guarding them with humility brings nobility.
If one's people are numerous and one's soldiers are strong,
guarding them with caution brings victory.
If one is intelligent and wise,
guarding these traits with seeming foolishness brings sagacity.
If one is broadly learned and has a strong memory,
guarding these traits with seeming shallowness prevents overflowing.
These six,
all are virtues of humility.
The *Yì* says:
“Humility brings success;
the superior man brings things to a good conclusion. Good fortune.”
To be able to end with good fortune
is the way of the superior man.
Though noble as the Son of Heaven,
and wealthy, possessing all within the four seas,
yet without the virtue of humility,
thus losing their lives,
Jié and Zhòu are examples of this,
and how much more so common people?
Now, the *Yì* has one principle,
which is great enough to govern the world,
moderate enough to secure the family and state,
and near enough to preserve one’s own person;
this is none other than the virtue of humility!"

Heaven is one,
earth is two,
Humans: three.
Three times three is nine.

The rest are each according to their kind.
Birds and fish are both born in the yin and belong to the yang,

Fish swim in the water,
birds fly in the clouds.

and transform into crabs (
The natures of all things are of different kinds.
Therefore, silkworms eat but do not drink,

mayflies neither drink nor eat.
Shellfish and scaled creatures eat in summer and hibernate in winter.
Those that gnaw and swallow have eight orifices and are born from eggs.

Those with four feet have no feathers or wings.
Those that bear horns have no upper teeth.

Those with feathers have grease but no back teeth.
Those born in the day resemble the father.

In general, east and west directions on the earth are called wěi (緯, latitude),

Mountains accumulate virtue,

The prosperity and decline of bàng (蜯, large clams), há (蛤, clams), turtles, and pearls

Therefore, people who eat from firm soil are fat,
people who eat from loose soil are large,
people who eat from sandy soil are thin,

Therefore it is said:
Among the three hundred and sixty kinds of winged creatures,

among the three hundred and sixty kinds of furry creatures,

Of the 360 creatures with shells

Of the 360 creatures with scales

These are the beautiful categories of Heaven and Earth
, the numbers of birds, beasts, and all things.
Therefore, if emperors love to destroy nests and break eggs

if they love to disembowel fetuses and kill the premature

Therefore, the actions of a king must be according to the Dao

If action is not according to the Dao
, and stillness is not according to principle

Monstrous omens will frequently arise

The people will die young

"The six domestic animals do not flourish."

*Shuō Yuàn · Fǎn Zhì* 《說苑·反質》: Confucius 孔子 cast the hexagram *Bì* 賁,
sighed and looked up,
feeling uneasy.

raised his hand and asked,
"Master, I have heard that *Bì* 賁 is an auspicious hexagram,
why do you sigh at it?"
Confucius 孔子 said,
"Bì
is not a primary color,
therefore one sighs over it.
I admire that which is genuine and unadorned;
white should be truly white,
black should be truly black.
What need is there for embellishment?
I have also heard it said:
Red lacquer requires no decoration,
white jade requires no carving,
precious pearls require no adornment.
Why is this?
It is because their inherent quality is sufficient and needs no further embellishment."
*Huáinánzi · Rénjiān Xùn* Kǒngzǐ, upon reading the *Yìjīng* concerning the hexagrams *Sǔn* (Decrease) and *Yì* (Increase),
never failed to sigh with indignation, saying:
"Decrease and Increase,
are they not matters for rulers?
Affairs are sometimes intended to benefit,
but instead only serve to harm;
sometimes intended to harm,
but instead bring benefit.
The reversal of benefit and harm
is the gateway to disaster and fortune,
and cannot be left unexamined."
*Shuō Yuàn · Jìng Shèn* Kǒngzǐ, upon reading the *Yìjīng* concerning the hexagrams *Sǔn* and *Yì*,
sighed deeply.
Zǐxià, avoiding his seat, asked,
"Why does the Master sigh?"
Confucius said,
"Those who diminish themselves increase,
those who increase themselves diminish;
it is for this reason that I sigh."
Zixia said,
"In that case, is it not permissible for a student to increase?"
Confucius said,
"No.
The Way of Heaven
is that those who achieve are never able to maintain it for long.
A student receives knowledge with emptiness,
therefore it is said he gains.
If one does not know how to avoid being full,
then all the good words in the world cannot enter his ears.
In the past, Yao held the position of Son of Heaven,
yet he was still sincerely respectful in maintaining it,
and remained empty and quiet to await the submissions of his inferiors.
Therefore, after a hundred years he became even more prosperous,
and to this day his virtue is ever more evident.
Kunwu praised himself and was complacent,
reached the pinnacle and did not decline,
therefore he failed and was defeated in his own time,
and to this day his wickedness has increased.
Are these not signs of diminution and increase?
Therefore, I say,
humility
is the means of expressing respect and preserving one's position.
Abundant light moves,
Therefore, one can become great.
If one becomes great, then one becomes deficient.
I warn against it.
Therefore, it is said that the good words of the world cannot enter his ears.
When the sun is at its zenith, it declines;
when the moon is full, it wanes.
Heaven and earth experience fullness and emptiness,
increasing and decreasing with time.
Therefore, the sage dares not accept prosperity.
When ascending a carriage and encountering three people, he alights;
encountering two people, he bows on the carriage.
He regulates his fullness and emptiness,
therefore he can endure for a long time."
Zǐ Xià said,
"Good.
I will recite this for the rest of my life."
*Lùn Héng · Bǔ Shì* Zǐ Lù asked Kǒngzǐ, saying:

the meaning of "龜" (guī) is "old" (舊, jiù).
To clarify matters of doubt and confusion,
"[You] should ask the elders and former officials."

*Shàngshū Dàzhuàn · Lüèshuō* Zǐ Xià finished reading the *Shū* (Book of Documents),
and went to see the Master.
The Master asked him:
"What did you learn from the *Shū*?"
Zǐ Xià 子夏 replied,
"The way the *Book of Documents* discusses affairs
is as clear and bright as the sun and moon succeeding each other in illuminating,
as distinctly arranged as the stars and constellations in their courses.
Above, it contains the Way of Yáo 堯 and Shùn 舜;
below, it contains the righteousness of the Three Kings.
What Shāng 商 (Zǐ Xià 子夏's personal name) received from you, Master,
I have inscribed upon my heart,
daring not to forget it.
Even if I were to retreat and dwell among the rocks, between the Yellow River and the Jì 濟 River,
in the depths of the mountains,
making broken dwellings,
and weaving rough brushwood doors,
I would still play the zither within them,
using it to sing the airs of the Former Kings.
Then I could give vent to my pent-up feelings with fervor,
forgetting my own poverty and lowliness.
If there were someone, I would also rejoice;
if there were no one, I would also rejoice,
and unknowingly forget worries, troubles, and death."
The Master, looking impressed, changed his expression and said,
"Ah!
You are almost worthy to discuss the *Book of Documents* with me.
However,
you have seen its exterior,
but not yet seen its interior."
Yán Yuān 顏淵 asked,
"What do you mean?"
The Master said:
"Peeking at its gate without entering within,
how can one observe where its profound treasures lie?
Yet hiding them is not difficult.
I, Qiū, once devoted my mind and will to enter its principles,
only to find a high bank in front
and a great stream behind,
standing perfectly upright, staunch and unwavering.
Therefore, the Yáo Diǎn can be used to observe beauty,
the Yǔ Gòng can be used to observe accomplishments,
Jiù Yáo can be used to observe governance,
the Hóng Fàn can be used to observe standards,
the Liù Shì can be used to observe righteousness,
the Wǔ Gào can be used to observe benevolence,
and the Fǔ Xíng can be used to observe warnings.
By understanding these seven observations,
the grand principles of the *Book of Documents* are grasped."
*Han Poetry Outer Commentary* 2. Zǐ Xià finished reading the *Book of Poetry*.
The Master asked,
"What do you find so great about the *Book of Poetry*?"
Zǐ Xià replied,
"The *Book of Poetry*, regarding affairs,
shines brightly like the light of the sun and moon,
radiates brilliantly like the orderly movement of the stars and constellations.
Above, it contains the ways of Yáo and Shùn;
below, it contains the righteousness of the Three Kings.
I, your disciple, dare not forget them.
Even if I live in a humble cottage,
playing the zither and chanting the airs of the former kings,
whether someone enjoys it or
no one enjoys it, I still enjoy it.
It can also inspire me to forget to eat.
The *Shī* (Book of Poetry) says:
"Beneath the rough gate,
one can rest and linger;
The Mì River flows wide,
it can cure hunger."
Fūzǐ suddenly changed his expression and said:
"Ah!
My son, you can probably discuss the *Shī* now.
However, you have only seen its surface;
you have not seen its essence."
Yán Yuān said:
"The surface has already been seen;
what else is there to its essence?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Peeking at the door without entering,
how can you know where the hidden depths lie?
However, the hiding place is not difficult [to find].
Qiū once focused my mind and exhausted my will to enter it completely.
In front, there is a high bank;
behind, there is a deep valley.
It stands serenely, thus established.
Not being able to see its essence
means one cannot be called refined and subtle."
*Shuō Yuàn·Jìng Shèn* Kǒngzǐ said:
Survival, extinction, disaster, and fortune,
all lie within oneself.
Natural disasters and earthly anomalies
also cannot kill one.
In the past, during the time of the Yīn king, Dì Xīn,
a sparrow grew into a crow in the corner of the city.
The artisans divined it, saying:
"Whenever something small grows into something large,
the state will surely be blessed,
and the king's name will surely be doubled."
Dì Xīn rejoiced in the virtue of the sparrow,
did not govern the state,
and was excessively violent without limit.
External enemies then arrived,
and consequently the Yīn state was destroyed.
This was a time of opposing Heaven,
and a false blessing turned into disaster.
As for the time of the Yīn king, Wǔ Dīng,
the ways of the former kings were lacking,
and penal laws were lax.
A mulberry and a paper mulberry both grew in the court,
and in seven days grew to be as large as an embrace.
The artisans divined it, saying:
"The mulberry and paper mulberry
are wild things.
Wild things growing in the court,
does it mean the court will perish?"
Wǔ Dīng was fearful and alarmed,
Cultivating oneself while living in seclusion,
contemplating the policies of the former kings,
reviving states that had been extinguished,
continuing lines of succession that had been broken,
promoting worthy men who had been living in obscurity,
and clarifying the principles of caring for the elderly.
After three years,
rulers from distant lands,
came to court through multiple interpreters; there were six such states.
This was in accordance with the timing of Heaven,
and disaster was transformed into blessing.
Therefore, anomalies and prodigies
are what Heaven uses to warn the Son of Heaven and the feudal lords;
bad dreams
are what are used to warn scholar-officials.
Therefore, anomalies and prodigies cannot overcome good governance,
and bad dreams cannot overcome good conduct.
At the height of perfect governance,
disaster is transformed into blessing.
Therefore, Tài Jiǎ said:
"Calamities sent by Heaven,
may still be avoided;
but calamities brought on by oneself,
cannot be escaped."

*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn*, 5. Zǐ Xià asked,
"Why does 'Guān Jū' begin the *Guó Fēng* section?"
Confucius said,
"How profound is the 'Guān Jū'!
The person in the 'Guān Jū',
looks up to Heaven,
and bows down to Earth.
In the profound and obscure,
it is where virtue is stored;
in the bustling and teeming,
it is where the Way is practiced.
It is like the transformations of a divine dragon,
displaying brilliant patterns.
How great!
The Way of 'Guān Jū'!
It is what all things depend on,
and what all living beings rely on for their lives.
The River Lúo produces writing and diagrams,
and the lín and fèng birds soar in the suburbs.
If not following the Way of 'Guān Jū',
then how could the matters of 'Guān Jū' ever be achieved?
The strategies of the Six Classics,
all come down to diligent discourse,
ultimately deriving from 'Guān Jū'.
The affairs of 'Guān Jū' are of great importance!
Assisting and supporting,
from east to west,
from south to north,
there is no thought that does not submit.
You must strive for it,
and contemplate it.
Among Heaven and Earth,
all the kinds of living beings,
the origin of the kingly way,
nothing is beyond this!"
Zǐ Xià, sighing deeply, said:
"How great is the *Guān Jū*!
It is the foundation of Heaven and Earth."
*Lǚshì Chūnqiū · Jìchūn Jì · Xiān Jǐ* The *Shī* says:
"Holding the reins as if threading silk."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"If one understands these words,
one can govern the world."
Zǐgòng said:

Kǒngzǐ said:
"It is not about being hasty,

*Yántiě Lùn · Xiāng Cì* Kǒngzǐ said:
"The poets are vexed that they cannot be silent,
and Qiū is vexed that he cannot remain hidden."
Therefore, traveling east, west, south, and north,
presenting seventy theories that were not adopted,
he then retreated and cultivated the kingly way,
composing the *Chūnqiū*,
to bequeath it to ten thousand generations hence,
for the world to find its balance in it.
*Lùnhéng · Duì Zuò* Kǒngzǐ said:
"Poets resent not being able to remain silent,
and Qiū (丘) resents not being able to remain hidden."
This is the argument.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"In the breadth of the Hé (河),
I recognize the perfection of virtue.
If you wish to attain it,
each must return to its origin,
and revert to the ways of antiquity."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"In the *Gān Táng* (甘棠) I see the reverence for the ancestral temple.
To greatly honor a person,
one must respect their position.
By harmonizing and securing all things,
the way of the ancient sages is nearly attained!"
Kǒngzǐ, discussing the *Shī* (詩, Book of Poetry),
upon reaching the sixth chapter of "Zhēng Yuè" (正月),
fearfully said:
"An upright man who does not encounter the right time,
how can he not be in danger!
Following superiors and conforming to the world means abandoning the Dao;
opposing superiors and separating from custom means endangering oneself.
When the world does not align with goodness,
and one alone follows it,
then one will be called either a monster or a prodigy.
This is why Jié (桀) killed Guān Lóngféng (關龍逢),
and Zhòu (紂) killed Prince Bǐgān (比干).
Therefore, when a worthy person does not encounter the right time,
they are constantly afraid they will not see it through to the end.
The *Shī* says:
"Although we say Heaven is high,
we dare not but be cautious;
although we say Earth is thick,
we dare not but tread carefully."
This is what it means.
*Hàn Shū·Liú Xiàng Zhuàn* Confucius, discussing the *Shī*,
upon reaching "the Yin officers are clever and quick,
they will pour libations in the capital,"
sighed and said:
"Great is the Mandate of Heaven!
Goodness must be passed on to descendants.
Therefore, wealth and rank are not constant.
If it were not so,
how would kings and dukes be warned and careful!
How would the common people be encouraged!"
*Máo Shī·Sù Guān Zhuàn* After Zǐxià finished his three-year mourning period,

Fūzǐ said:
"Zǐxià's sorrow has already been fully expressed,
and he can guide it to accord with the rites,
therefore I say he is a Jūnzǐ;
Mǐn Zǐqiān's sorrow is not yet fully expressed,
but he can restrain himself with the rites,
therefore I say he is a Jūnzǐ.
The three-year mourning period
is what the worthy consider light,
and what the unworthy strive for."
*Huáinánzǐ·Miù Chēng Xùn*. Mǐn Zǐqiān finished the three-year mourning period,
he took up the qín and tuned its strings,
its sound was earnest and sorrowful.
Fūzǐ said:
"The tuning is correct,
but the sound is not."
*Shuō Yuàn·Xiū Wén*. Zǐxià finished the three-year mourning period,
and was seen by Kǒngzǐ.
Kǒngzǐ gave him a zither,
and asked him to string it.
He took the zither and strung it,
playing happily and cheerfully.
Then he stood up and said:
"The former kings established ritual,
I dare not fall short of it."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"He is a junzi."
After Mǐn Zǐqiān completed the three-year mourning period,
he met with Kǒngzǐ.
Kǒngzǐ gave him a zither,
and asked him to string it.
He took the zither and strung it,
playing sadly and mournfully.
Then he stood up and said:
"The former kings established ritual,
I dare not exceed it."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"He is a junzi."
Zǐgòng asked:
"Mǐnzi's sorrow was not fully expressed,
yet you said 'He is a junzi';
Zǐxià's sorrow was fully expressed,
yet you said 'He is a junzi.'
Cì is confused,
may I ask what you mean?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
Mǐn Zǐ's sorrow was not fully expressed,
but he could curtail it with propriety;
therefore, he is called a gentleman.
Zǐ Xià's sorrow was fully expressed,
but he could draw it out and extend it;
therefore, he is called a gentleman.
The three-year mourning period
is certainly a compromise for those who are superior,
and an exertion for those who are inferior."
*Later Han, Biography of Zhāng Fèn* Kǒngzǐ said to Zǐ Xià:
"Propriety is for cultivating the external,
music is for cultivating the internal.
I am finished!"
*Records of the Elder Dai: Duke Ai Asked* Duke Ai asked Kǒngzǐ, saying:
"What is the great propriety like?
The gentleman's discussion of propriety,
why is it so highly regarded?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"I am but a small man,
how could I possibly know propriety!"
The Duke said:
"No.
Please, Master, speak of it."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"I have heard that
for the people, that from which they are born,
propriety is the greatest.
Without propriety, there is no way to regulate the service to the spirits of Heaven and Earth.
Without ritual propriety (lǐ), there is no way to distinguish the positions of ruler and subject, superior and inferior, elder and younger.
Without ritual propriety, there is no way to differentiate the intimacy between male and female, father and son, brothers, or the closeness or distance in marriage and social relationships.
The noble person (jūnzǐ) regards these things as deserving of respect,
and then uses their abilities to teach the common people,
not neglecting the occasions for gatherings and festivals.
When something is accomplished,
then they regulate the carving, engraving, decorative patterns, and embroidery to pass them on to posterity.
When the natural order is followed,
then they speak of mourning calculations,
prepare the sacrificial tripods and dishes,
set out the pig offerings for the winter sacrifice,
maintain their ancestral temples,
and reverently perform sacrifices at fixed times throughout the year,
to maintain order within the kinship.
Then they secure their dwellings,
make plain their clothing,
keep their palaces modest,
the carriages are without carved decorations,
the utensils are not elaborately engraved,
the food does not consist of two courses,
sharing benefits with the people.
This is how the noble people of the past practiced ritual propriety."
The Duke said,
"The noble people of today,
why do they not practice it?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"The noble people of today,
are insatiable in their love of beauty,
Excessive in immoral behavior without tiring,
negligent, lazy, and arrogant,
determined to exhaust the people,
opposing the multitude to attack those who possess the Dao,
seeking to obtain what one desires,
not by proper means.
In ancient times, those who employed the people led from the front;
nowadays, those who employ the people lag behind.
The gentlemen of today no longer practice propriety."
Kǒngzǐ was sitting in attendance upon Āigōng.
Āigōng said,
"May I venture to ask, what is of greatest importance in the way of humankind?"
Kǒngzǐ looked grave and replied,
"Your lord asking about this is a virtue of the common people,
so how could your minister dare to decline to answer?
The way of humankind,
governance is of the greatest importance."
Āigōng said,
"May I venture to ask, what is meant by 'governance'?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"Governance is
correctness.
If the ruler is correct,
then the people will follow in correctness.
What the ruler does,
the people will follow;
what the ruler does not do,
how can the people follow?"
"Where should the common people follow?"
The Duke said:
"May I venture to ask, what is governing like?"
Kǒngzǐ replied:
"Husband and wife should have their distinct roles,
father and son should be close,
the ruler and his ministers should be dignified.
If these three are correct,
then the common people will follow."
The Duke said:
"Although I am not worthy,
I would like to hear how to implement the way of these three sayings.
Is it possible to hear about it?"
Kǒngzǐ replied:
"In ancient governance,
loving the people was paramount;
in order to govern and love the people,
ritual was paramount;
in order to govern ritual,
reverence was paramount;
and the utmost of reverence,
the great marriage was paramount.
The great marriage is the utmost,
the great marriage having reached its utmost,
wearing the冕(miǎn) and personally welcoming the bride,
is to show affection.
Showing affection,
is to show affection.
Therefore, the junzi (君子) cultivates reverence to show affection for relatives;
to abandon reverence is to neglect one's relatives.
Without love, one cannot be close;
without reverence, one cannot be correct.
Love and reverence,
are they not the foundation of government!"
The Duke said:
"I wish to say something.
To wear the mian (冕) and personally greet the bride,
is that not excessively important?"
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) looked grave and changed his expression, replying:
"To unite the goodness of two surnames,
to continue the posterity of the former sages,
to provide the master of Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temple,
how can Your Lordship consider this excessively important?"
The Duke said:
"I am indeed foolish.
If I were not foolish,
how could I have heard these words?
I wanted to ask,
but could not find the words.
Please advance the discussion further."
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"If Heaven and Earth do not combine,
the myriad things cannot be born.
The great marriage
is the succession for ten thousand generations.
How can Your Lordship consider it excessively important?"
Kǒngzǐ then had this to say:
"Inwardly, if one governs the rites of the ancestral temple,
it is sufficient to be matched with the spirits of Heaven and Earth.
Outwardly, if one governs the rites of upright speech,
it is sufficient to establish respect between superiors and inferiors.
Shaming things is sufficient to uplift them;
shaming the state is sufficient to revitalize it.
Governing begins with ritual;
ritual
is the root of governance!"
Kǒngzǐ then said:
"In the past, the governance of the enlightened kings of the Three Dynasties
certainly showed reverence for their wives and children, and there was a proper way to do so.
The wife
is the head of the family;
how dare one not respect her?
The son
is the continuation of the parents;
how dare one not respect him?
The noble person has nothing that he does not respect,
but respecting oneself is the greatest.
The self
is a branch of the parents;
how dare one not respect it?
If one cannot respect oneself,
it is harming one's parents.
Harming one's parents
is harming the root;
If the root is injured,
the branches will consequently wither and die.
These three
are analogous to the common people.
Oneself and one's own person,
one's children and one's children,
one's spouse and one's spouse—
if the superior man conducts himself according to these three,
then he will inspire the whole world!
The way of Tàiwáng is like this,
and the state will be harmonious."
The Duke said,
"May I ask what is meant by 'revering oneself'?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"If the superior man's words are excessive,
the people will compose eloquent speeches;
if his actions are excessive,
the people will create rules and precedents.
If the superior man's words do not exceed proper diction,
and his actions do not exceed proper standards,
the people will be respectful and reverent without being commanded.
If this is so,
then he can revere himself;
if he can revere himself,
then he can perfect his parents."
The Duke said,
"May I ask what is meant by 'perfecting one's parents'?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"What is a Jūnzǐ?
It is the fulfillment of a person's reputation.
When the common people attribute a good name to someone,
calling them the son of a Jūnzǐ,
they are thereby causing their parents to be regarded as Jūnzǐ as well.
This is to fulfill the reputation of their parents."
Kǒngzǐ then said:
"In ancient governance,
loving the people was paramount.
If one cannot love the people,
one cannot possess oneself.
If one cannot possess oneself,
one cannot secure the land.
If one cannot secure the land,
one cannot find joy in Heaven.
If one cannot find joy in Heaven,
one cannot fulfill oneself."
The Duke said:
"May I venture to ask, what does it mean to fulfill oneself?"
Kǒngzǐ replied:
"Not being overcome by material possessions."
The Duke said:
"May I venture to ask, what does a Jūnzǐ value in the Way of Heaven?"
Kǒngzǐ replied:
"They value its ceaselessness,
like the sun and moon following each other from west to east without end,
this is the Way of Heaven.
Not shutting off its permanence,
This is the way of Heaven;
accomplishing things without action,
this is the way of Heaven;
completing and enlightening,
this is the way of Heaven."
The Duke said:
"I, your servant, am foolish, ignorant, and troubled,
you understand this in your heart."
Kǒngzǐ hastily stepped down from his mat and replied:
"A benevolent person does not overstep the bounds of things,
a filial son does not overstep the bounds of things,
thus, the benevolent person serves his parents as he serves Heaven,
serving Heaven as he serves his parents,
therefore, the filial son completes himself."
The Duke said:
"Now that I have heard these words,
what about future transgressions?"
Kǒngzǐ replied:
"That Your Lordship considers these words
is a blessing for your servant."
*Gǔliáng Zhuàn*, Year 3 of Duke Huán Zǐgòng said: "To wear the ceremonial cap and personally greet the bride,
isn't that excessively formal?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"To unite the goodness of two surnames
in order to continue the posterity of ten thousand generations,
how can you say that it is excessively formal?"
*Dà Dài Lǐ · Lǐ Chá* Kǒngzǐ said:
"The Way of the gentleman,
Is it like a dike?"
The blockage of ritual
is where disorder arises,
just as the blockage of a dike
is where water comes from.
Therefore, those who consider old dikes useless and destroy them
will surely suffer from water damage.
Those who consider old rituals useless and abandon them
will surely suffer from the calamity of disorder.
Therefore, if the rites of marriage are abandoned,
then the way of husband and wife will be fraught with hardship, and the crimes of adultery and perversion will be many.
If the rites of village drinking are abandoned,
then the order of elders and juniors will be lost, and the lawsuits of contention and fighting will be numerous.
If the rites of betrothal and archery are abandoned,
then the actions of the feudal lords will be evil, and the disasters of excess and overflowing will arise.
If the rites of mourning and sacrifice are abandoned,
then the kindness of ministers and sons will be thin, and the rituals of turning one's back on death and forgetting life will be numerous.
In general, human knowledge
can see what has already happened,
but cannot see what will happen.
Rituals
prohibit things before they are about to happen;
while laws
prohibit things after they have already happened.
Therefore, the use of law is easy to see,
but the reasons for the existence of ritual are difficult to know.
As for celebrating rewards to encourage good,
and using punishments to deter evil,
The former kings held to this principle of correctness,
firm as metal and stone.
They practiced this trustworthiness,
as compliant as the four seasons.
They conducted this meritorious service,
as impartial as Heaven and Earth.
How could you dare not to use it?
However, as the saying goes, "ritual, ritual,"
it values cutting off evil before it sprouts and generating respect in the minute and subtle,
so that the people daily move toward goodness and away from sin without even knowing it."
"Shēn once heard the Master say:
'The Dao of Heaven is called round,
the Dao of Earth is called square.
Square is called dark, and round is called bright.
Brightness
is that which emits qi,
therefore it reflects outward;
darkness
is that which contains qi,
therefore it reflects inward.'"
*Bái Hǔ Tōng·Shèjì* Zēngzǐ asked,
"When feudal lords are sacrificing to the gods of soil and grain,
and the sacrificial vessels are already arranged,
[and they] hear of the Son of Heaven's death,
what should they do?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Stop.
The ministers and sons grieved painfully,
not daring to conclude the rites in the usual way."
*Bái Hǔ Tōng - Fēng Gōng Hóu* Zēng Zǐ asked,
"Establishing the heir based on seniority and not virtue, why is that?"
"Because determining virtue and lack thereof based on words
is impossible to know."
*Bái Hǔ Tōng - Jià Qǔ* Zēng Zǐ asked,
"In marriage rites,
after the betrothal gifts have been presented,
and an auspicious day has been chosen,
if the bride's parents die,
what should be done?"
Kǒng Zǐ said,
"The groom should send someone to offer condolences.
If the groom's parents die,
the bride should also send someone to offer condolences,
referring to the father in case of the father's death,
and the mother in case of the mother's death.
If the parents are not alive,
then refer to the paternal uncle and the aunt.
After the groom is buried,
the groom's paternal uncle or paternal younger uncle should send someone to inform the bride's family, saying:
'So-and-so's son has the mourning of his parents,
and cannot continue as brothers [in the marriage].'
Send so-and-so to deliver the message,
and the bride's family agrees.
Not daring to marry [another],
is the proper etiquette.
After the groom has completed the mourning period,
the bride's father should send someone to inquire [about resuming the marriage].
Only after the groom does not take her as a wife can she marry someone else,
that is the proper etiquette.
If the bride's parents die,
the groom should do the same."
*Bái Hǔ Tōng · Sāngfú* Zēngzǐ asked,
"When the ruler dies and is already coffined,
and the subject has a parent's funeral,
what should be done?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Return home to reside.
If there is pressing business, then go to the ruler's place,
but not for morning and evening (rites)." He asked,
"When the ruler has been encoffined,
and the subject has a parent's funeral,
what should be done?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Return to encoffin and weep, then return to the ruler's place.
If there is pressing business, then return (home),
but not for morning and evening (rites).
The chamberlain of the grand master handles affairs,
and the scholar's sons and grandsons handle affairs.
If the wife has pressing business, then she also acts accordingly at the ruler's place,
but not for morning and evening (rites)."
*Bái Hǔ Tōng · Sāngfú* Zǐxià asked,
"After the three-year mourning period has concluded with the final cry,
those involved in military matters do not avoid it;
[Is this] ritual?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"I heard Lǎodān say:
'Lǔ Gōng Bóqín,
then there was action taken on his behalf.'
Now, taking advantage of the three-year mourning period for personal gain
shows ignorance."
*Hàn Shū·Yìwén Zhì*
Zhòngní said: "If ritual is lost, seek it among the common people."
*Hán Fēi Zi·Wài Chǔ Shuō Zuǒ Xià*
Kǒngzǐ was sitting in attendance upon Lǔ Āigōng.
Āigōng bestowed upon him peaches and millet.
Āigōng requested its use.
Kǒngzǐ first ate the millet and then ate the peach.
Those on the left and right all covered their mouths and laughed.
Āigōng said:
"Millet is not for eating as food,
it is for cleansing the peach."
Zhòngní replied:
"Qiū knows this.
Millet is the chief of the five grains,
offered to the ancestral kings as the finest offering.
Of the six fruits and melons, the peach is the lowest,
and is not allowed in the ancestral temple when offering sacrifices to the former kings.
Qiū has heard that
a gentleman uses the lowly to cleanse the esteemed;
he has not heard of using the esteemed to cleanse the lowly.
Now, to use the chief of the five grains to cleanse the lowest of fruits and melons
This is like snow falling from above.
Qiū (丘, likely referring to Kǒngzǐ 孔子) believed it hinders righteousness,
therefore he dared not prioritize it over the grand ceremonies of the ancestral temple.
*Lǚshì Chūnqiū · Mèngdōng Jì · Ān Sǐ*: When the Lǔ (魯) state's Jìsūn (季孫) family had a funeral,
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) went to offer condolences.
Entering the gate, he went to the left,
behaving as a guest.
The host used *yúfán* (璵璠, a type of jade) to collect [offerings],
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) went straight to the courtyard and hurried forward,
ascending the steps, and said:
"Using precious jade for collection [offerings],
is like exposing a corpse in the Central Plains."
*Huáinánzǐ · Miù Chēng Xùn*: Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"When Jūn (鈞) cried, he said:
'What shall I do, Zǐ Yǔ (子予)? What shall I ride?'
The sorrow was the same,
but the reasons for their sorrow were different.
Therefore, sorrow and joy deeply affect human emotions."
*Shuō Yuàn · Xiū Wén*: Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"To change customs and transform habits,
nothing is better than music;
to pacify superiors and govern the people,
nothing is better than ritual."
Therefore, the sage kings cultivated ritual and culture,
established schools,
displayed bells and drums.
The Son of Heaven had the Bìyōng (辟雍),
the feudal lords had the Pàngōng (泮宮),
Therefore, practice virtue and transform others.
*Shuō Yuàn · Xiū Wén*: Confucius said:
"Rituals without physical form
are respectful;
mourning without mourning garments
is sorrowful;
music without sound
is joyful;
trustworthiness without speaking,
authority without movement,
benevolence without bestowing,
is intention.
The sound of bells and drums,
if struck in anger, is martial;
if struck in sorrow, it is mournful;
if struck in joy, it is cheerful.
When the intention changes,
the sound also changes.
If the intention truly resonates with metal and stone,
how much more so with people!"
*Lùn Héng · Rú Zēng*: Confucius said:
"If words are not refined,
sometimes it is better not to speak."
*Lùn Héng · Shí Zhī*: Lǔ used wooden figures for burial,
and Confucius sighed.
*Shuǐ Jīng Zhù*, volume 6, quoting *Sāng Fú Yāo Jì*: Duke Āi of Lǔ was performing the ancestral sacrifice for his father.
Confucius asked,
"Would you rather set up a cassia tree?"
Āi Gōng said:
"No.
The guì (cinnamon) tree
originated with Jiè Zǐtuī.
Zǐtuī
was a man of Jìn.
Duke Wén experienced internal turmoil
and fled the country to the Dí people.
Zǐtuī followed him.
He cut flesh from his own body to sustain the army's provisions.
Later, Duke Wén restored the state
and unexpectedly forgot Zǐtuī.
Zǐtuī presented a song,
and Duke Wén finally realized [his oversight].
When he was about to receive rank and emolument,
Zǐtuī fled to Mount Jiè,
embraced a tree, and burned to death.
The people of the state buried him.
Fearing his spirit would burst forth from the earth,
they therefore made a guì tree.
My father was born in the palace
and died in his bed.
What use is a guì tree for him?"
*Yìwén Lèijù*, 85, quoting *Sāngfú Yāojì*. In the past, Duke Āi of Lǔ was carrying his father's coffin in a funerary cart.

Fearing their souls would be hungry,
they made the grain pouch.
My father died having tasted delicacies and been fed,

My father had none of Tài Bó's faults,

My father lived to receive sustenance,
"What is the reason for the Hétóng person?"
The *Yùlǎn*, volume 886, quotes the *Sāngfú Yāojì*: When Lǔ Āigōng buried his father,
Kǒngzǐ asked,

went to meet the corpse,
pitying the spirit's cold,
and therefore made a 'soul garment.'
My father wore brocade and embroidery while alive,
and died in clothes and bedding,
what need is there for a 'soul garment'?"
The *Yùlǎn*, volume 967, quotes the *Sāngfú Yāojì*: Once, Lǔ Āigōng was carrying his father's ancestral tablet (zǔzài).
Kǒngzǐ asked,

He replied,
"No.
'Peach soup' originated with Wèi Línggōng.
There was a woman being married off,
and her wet nurse accompanied the bride to her husband's home.
On the way, she heard that the husband had died.
The wet nurse wanted to take the bride back.
The bride said,

Now I belong to another.

"When one dies, one should exhaust sorrow."

and prepared a "three peach soup" to bathe the deceased.

"My father has nothing to regret,

*Lù Shǐ* (Road History), Later Records, Thirteen, commentary citing *Sāng Fú Yāo Jì* (Essentials of Mourning Attire): Duke Āi of Lǔ buried his father,

*Wǔ Xíng Dà Yì* (Great Meaning of the Five Elements), Four: Kǒngzǐ said,

*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn* (Han Interpretation of the Songs, Extraneous Chapters), Five: Kǒngzǐ was learning to play the *qín* from Shī Xiāngzǐ but did not progress.
Shī Xiāngzǐ said,
"Master, you may advance."
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Qiū has already grasped the tune,
but has not grasped its technique."
After a while, Shī Xiāngzǐ said,
"Master, you may advance." Kǒngzǐ said,
"Qiū has already grasped its technique,
but has not grasped its meaning."
After a while,
(Shī Xiāngzi) repeated,
"Master, you may proceed further." (Kǒngzǐ) said,
"Qiū has already grasped the person,
but has not yet grasped his character."
After a while, (Shī Xiāngzi) said,
"How distant is his far-reaching gaze,
how vast!
How dignified!
He must have composed this music.
Silently contemplating,
sorrowfully lamenting,
to rule the world,
to have the lords pay him court,
it can only be King Wén!"
Shī Xiāngzi withdrew from his mat, bowed twice, and said,
"Excellent.
Your teacher believes it is the *cāo* of King Wén."
Therefore, Kǒngzǐ, holding the sound of King Wén,
knew the person of King Wén.
Shī Xiāngzi said,
"May I venture to ask how you knew it was the *cāo* of King Wén?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Indeed.
The benevolent love greatness,
the harmonious love embellishment,
the wise love playing (music),
and those with earnest intentions love elegance.
It is through this that I, Qiū, understand the conduct of King Wén."
"Huáinánzǐ · Zhǔshù Xùn" Kǒngzǐ learned to play the qín from Shī Xiāng,
and understood the aspirations of King Wén,
seeing the subtle to know the obvious.
"Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn" 7 Once Kǒngzǐ played the sè,
Zēngzǐ and Zǐgòng listened attentively.
When the melody ended,
Zēngzǐ said:
"Alas!
The sound of the Master's sè seems to harbor a greedy and perverse heart,
how extremely unbenevolent and driven by profit it is!"
Zǐgòng thought so too,
and did not reply but went inside.
The Master saw that Zǐgòng had an expression of wanting to offer criticism,
a look of wanting to raise a difficulty,
so he put down the sè and waited for him.
Zǐgòng told him what Zēngzǐ had said.
The Master said:
"Alas!
Sēn,
is a worthy man in the world,
and indeed he is well-versed in music.
Formerly, Qiū (丘) was playing the zither,
and a mouse came out to play.
A wildcat appeared on the roof,
walking stealthily along the beam,
approaching it, then avoiding it,
with narrowed eyes and arched back,
searching but unable to find it.
Qiū (丘) used the zither to amplify its sound.
Sān (參) thought that Qiū (丘) was greedily perverse;
is it not fitting indeed!"
*Yù Lǎn* (禦覽) 81, quoting *Yuè Dòng Shēng Yí* (樂動聲儀). Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"The *Xiāo Sháo* (簫韶) music

Warm and harmonious,

*Hán Fēizǐ, Outer Congeries of Sayings, Left Below* Duke Āi of Lǔ asked Kǒngzǐ, saying:
"I have heard that in ancient times there was Kuí,
with one foot.
Is it really true that he had one foot?"
Kǒngzǐ answered, saying:
"No.
Kuí did not have one foot.
Kuí,
with an angry, violent, and wicked heart,
most people did not like to talk about him.
Although,
the reason why he was able to escape harm from others
was because of his trustworthiness.
People all said:
'Only this one thing is sufficient.'
Kuí did not have one foot,
but being single-minded was sufficient."
Duke Āi said:
"If that is truly the case, then it is indeed sufficient."
It is also said that
Duke Āi asked Kǒngzǐ, saying:
"I have heard that Kuí had one foot,
is it true?" He said:
"Kuí
was a person.
Why did he have only one foot?
He had no other extraordinary qualities,
but was uniquely accomplished in music.
Yáo said:
'Kuí alone is sufficient.'
He appointed him as the director of music.
Therefore, the superior man said:
'Kuí has one foot.'
It is not that he had only one foot."
*Lǚshì Chūnqiū · Shènxíng Lùn · Chá Zhuàn* Duke Āigōng of Lǔ asked Confucius, saying:
"The director of music, Kuí, had one foot.
Is this true?"
Confucius said:
"In the past,
Shùn desired to use music to spread instruction throughout the world.
He ordered Chónglí to find Kuí from the midst of the wilderness and present him.
Shùn made him the director of music.
Thereupon Kuí rectified the six pitch pipes,
harmonized the five tones,
and regulated the eight winds,
and the world was greatly subdued.
Chónglí wanted to seek even more men,
but Shùn said:
'Music
is the essence of heaven and earth,
and the regulation of gain and loss.
Therefore, only the sage is capable of being the source of harmony and music.
Kuí was able to harmonize it,
in order to pacify the world.
Someone like Kuí,
one is enough."
Therefore, it is said that Kuí had one foot;
it is not that he had one foot.”
*Huáinánzǐ·Zhǔ Shù Xùn* Furthermore, Róng Qǐqī played the instrument once,

*Shuō Yuàn·Xiū Wén* Zǐlù played the zither with sounds of the northern frontier.
Kǒngzǐ heard it and said,
“Indeed!
Yóu is truly untalented.”
Rǎn Yǒu was attending.
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Qiú! Come here.
Why don't you tell Yóu?
The ancient kings, in creating music,
played central notes,
to create moderate rhythms,
flowing into the south,
not returning to the north.
The south
is the region of growth and nurturing;
the north
is the domain of killing and destruction.
Therefore, the superior man holds the center as his foundation,
and strives for life as his base.
Therefore, its sound is gentle and harmonious and resides in the center,
to symbolize the qi of growth and nurturing.
Feelings of worry, sorrow, and pain
are not added to the heart,
and violent, fierce, unrestrained and wild impulses
are not present in the body.
Such being the case,
this is the manner of survival and order,
and the means of peace and joy.
But petty people are not like this.
They grasp the trivial and debate the fundamental,
making rigidity the foundation.
Therefore, their tone is shrill, harsh, and superficial,
symbolizing the qi of killing and warfare.
Feelings of harmony, moderation, and correctness
do not burden the mind;
warm, dignified, respectful, and proper actions
are not present in the body.
For killing
is the manner of chaos and ruin,
and the means of fleeing in defeat.
In the past, Shùn created the sounds of the Southern Wind;
his rise to power was sudden and vigorous.
Even now, kings and dukes follow it and do not abandon it.
Zhòu made the sounds of the Northern Border;
his downfall was swift and sudden.
Even now, kings and dukes laugh at it.
Shùn, though a commoner,
accumulated righteousness and embodied benevolence,
practiced moderation and performed good deeds,
and ultimately rose to prominence.
Zhòu, though an emperor,
was fond of arrogance, licentiousness, and recklessness,
was unyielding, harsh, violent, and thieving,
and ultimately met his demise.
Now, Yóu,
is a commoner,
a despicable fellow in plain clothes.
He has no regard for the systems of the former kings,
and furthermore, has the tone of a state doomed to destruction.
How can he ensure the safety of his seven-foot body!"
Rǎn Yǒu told Zǐlù about this,
Zǐlù said:
"It is Yóu's fault.
A petty person cannot avoid being trapped and drawn into this;
it is fitting that the Master would say this."
Thereupon, he regretted his actions,
and refrained from eating.
After seven days, he was skin and bones.
Confucius said:
"Yóu has corrected his faults."

*Shuō Yuàn · Zhìgōng* Master Kǒng traveled,

so he withdrew and revised the *Chūnqiū*.
He collected the goodness of even the finest hair,

Human affairs were thoroughly examined,
and the way of the king was made complete.
This refined harmony and sagely creation
communicated with Heaven, and the qílín arrived.
This was Heaven's recognition of the Master.
Thereupon, he sighed and said:
"Is Heaven, with its ultimate clarity, not to be obscured?

Is Earth, with its ultimate stability, not to be endangered?

then it is because worthy sages speak to the world but are unable to implement their ways,
Therefore, disasters and anomalies occur together."
