are beautiful jade; *wú*,
is three-colored jade;
*líng*, *qiāng*, *chēng*, *suǒ*, and *huáng*,
are sounds of jade; *niè*,
is a jade pendant; *jiǎo*,
are earplugs; *sào*,
is jade ornaments with water chestnut patterns."
*Chū Xué Jì* 27. The *Yì Lúnyǔ* says:
Fán yú,
are precious jades of Lǔ.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"How beautiful is fán yú!
Viewed from afar,
it appears brilliant;
viewed up close,
it appears serene.
One aspect emphasizes its texture,
the other emphasizes its genuineness."
*Wén Xuǎn*, Liú Xīn's "Letter to the Grand Master of Ceremonies" commentary quotes the *Lúnyǔ Chèn*. After returning from Wèi to Lǔ,
he edited the *Shī* and *Shū*,
and revised the *Chūnqiū*.
*Wén Xuǎn*, "Stele Inscription of the King of Qí Ānlù" commentary quotes the *Lúnyǔ Chèn*. Zhòngní resided in his village,
cherishing virtuous principles.
*Shuōwén*. Kǒngzǐ said:
"Unifying three into one makes a king."
*Shuōwén*. Kǒngzǐ said:
"Combining ten into one makes a shì (gentleman)."
*Shuōwén*. Kǒngzǐ said:
"Wū (烏, crow),
is a hū (盱) sound.
It is used to assist the breath,
therefore it is used as wū hū (烏呼, alas)."
*Shuōwén*. Kǒngzǐ said:
"The characters for 'cow' and 'sheep'
are based on their shapes."
*Shuōwén*. Kǒngzǐ said:
"Shǔ (黍) can be made into wine;
hé (禾) enters water."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Sù (粟) means to continue."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Being beneath people,
hence it is bent and crooked."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Mò (貉) means evil."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Looking at the character for 'dog' (犬),
it's like a drawing of a dog."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Gǒu (狗) means
to knock.
It knocks the air, barks, and guards."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"The Six Arts, in governance,
are one.
*Lǐ* (禮, Ritual) regulates people,
*Yuè* (樂, Music) promotes harmony,
*Shū* (書, Writing) conveys matters,
*Shī* (詩, Poetry) expresses intentions,
*Yì* (易, Change) deals with spiritual transformation,
*Chūnqiū* (春秋, Spring and Autumn Annals) uses righteousness."
Kǒngzǐ lived in the declining years of the Zhōu dynasty,
when the Kingly Way was decaying,
ritual and righteousness were abandoned and ruined,
The strong oppress the weak,
the many tyrannize the few.
The Son of Heaven does not dare to punish,
the regional lords do not dare to attack.
(He) lamented the failure of moral principles to be practiced,
therefore he traveled around responding to invitations,
hoping to implement his moral principles.
From Wèi he returned to Lǔ,
knowing he would not be employed,
therefore he finalized and established the Five Classics,
in order to practice his Dao.
*Lùnhéng · Yìwén* Emperor Xiàowǔ enfeoffed his younger brother as the Gong Prince of Lǔ.
The Gong Prince of Lǔ destroyed Kǒngzǐ's residence to build a palace,
and discovered lost *Shàngshū* in one hundred chapters,
*Lǐ* in three hundred,
*Chūnqiū* in thirty chapters,
*Lúnyǔ* in twenty-one chapters.
*Zhǔ Dé* Five [*Shàngshū Dàzhuàn*].
Wǔ Dīng sacrificed to Chéng Tāng.
A pheasant flew up to the ears of the cauldron and crowed.
Wǔ Dīng asked Zhǔ Jǐ about it.
Zhǔ Jǐ said:
"The pheasant
is a wild bird,
it should not ascend to the cauldron.
Now it ascends to the cauldron,
desiring to be employed.
Without this, might distant lands have those who come to court!"
Therefore Wǔ Dīng turned inward to examine himself,
in order to contemplate the Way of the former kings.
After three years,
those who braided their hair and came to court through multiple translations numbered six states.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"From the róng day sacrifice of Gāo Zōng,
I saw how quickly virtue is rewarded."
*Shàngshū Dàzhuàn·Lüèshuō* Kǒngzǐ said:
"The spirit of the heart is called sagehood."
*Shǐjì Bǔ·Sānhuáng Běnjì* citing *Hán Shī* Since ancient times, those who performed the fēng sacrifice at Mount Tài and the shàn sacrifice at Mount Liángfǔ
numbered more than ten thousand families.
Zhòngní observed them,
but could not fully recognize them all.
*Báihǔ Tōng·Fēngshàn* Kǒngzǐ said:
"Ascending Mount Tài,
observing the kings who changed surnames, one can count more than
seventy."
*Hán Shī Wàizhuàn* 3 King Zhuāng of Chǔ was seriously ill.
They divined about it, saying:
"The river is causing the trouble."
The senior official said:
"Please use sacrificial animals."
King Zhuāng said:
"Stop.
In ancient times, the sacrifices of the sage kings
did not exceed looking afar.
The Suī, Zhāng, Jiāng, and Hàn rivers
are what Chǔ looks afar to.
Though I did not obtain it,
the river is not the one to be blamed."
Consequently, he did not offer sacrifice.
After three days,
his illness began to abate.
Kǒngzǐ heard of this and said:
"The hegemony of King Zhuāng of Chǔ,
he certainly had a method for it.
Regulating his conduct and guarding his office,
examining himself without duplicity,
is it not fitting that he became a hegemon!"
King Zhāo of Chǔ fell ill,
and divined about it, saying:
"The river is the cause of the affliction."
The grand officers requested to use three sacrificial animals for it.
The king said:
"Stop.
In ancient times,
the former kings divided the land and established territories,
and their sacrifices did not exceed their domain.
The Jiāng, Hàn, Suī, and Zhāng Rivers
are within the domain of Chǔ.
If misfortune or blessings arrive,
it is not exceeding its domain.
Though I, being unworthy,
the river is not the one to be blamed."
Consequently, he did not offer sacrifice.
Zhòngní heard of this and said:
"King Zhāo (昭王) can be said to have understood the Way of Heaven.
It is fitting that he did not lose his state!"
*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn*, Seven. Confucius said:
"Enlightened rulers have three fears:
first, being in a high position and fearing that they will not hear their faults;
second, achieving their ambitions and fearing arrogance;
third, hearing the ultimate Way of the world and fearing that they will not be able to put it into practice."
*Dà Dài Lǐ · Zhǔ Yán*.
Confucius was at leisure,
and Zēng Zǐ (曾子) was attending him.
Confucius said,
"Cān (參),
the gentlemen of today are only between the words of the shì (士) and the dàfū (大夫);
those who reach the words of a true gentleman
are very rare.
Alas!
Will my words of a ruler die without being spoken?
How sad!"
Zēng Zǐ (曾子) rose and said,
"May I ask, what are the words of a ruler?"
Confucius did not answer.
Zēng Zǐ (曾子) was afraid,
respectfully adjusted his clothes, descended from his mat, and said,
"Your disciple knows his disrespect.
It is difficult to obtain the leisure of the Master,
therefore I dared to ask."
Confucius did not answer.
Zēng Zǐ was apprehensive.
He stepped back, leaned against the west wall, and stood there.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Shēn,
can you discuss the Way of an enlightened ruler?"
Zēng Zǐ said:
"I dare not consider myself sufficient.
It is difficult to receive leisure time from you, Master,
therefore I dare to ask."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"I will tell you.
The Way
is that by which virtue is illuminated;
virtue
is that by which the Way is honored.
Therefore, without virtue there is no honor,
without the Way there is no illumination.
Though one has state horses,
if they are not taught, they will not be obedient,
and one cannot travel a thousand *lǐ*.
Though one has broad lands and many people,
if one does not govern the land properly,
one cannot become a hegemonic ruler.
Therefore, the enlightened rulers of old
cultivated internally the Seven Teachings,
and practiced externally the Three Attainments.
If the Seven Teachings are cultivated, one can defend;
if the Three Attainments are practiced, one can conquer.
If the seven teachings are not cultivated,
even if one defends, it will not be secure;
if the three visits are not carried out,
even if one attacks, they will not submit.
Therefore, the defense of a wise ruler
must be to deter aggression a thousand *lǐ* away;
and their attack
is to return the army from the mat and seat.
Therefore, cultivate the seven teachings internally and the ruler will not be burdened;
carry out the three visits externally and wealth will not be wasted.
This is called the way of a wise ruler."
Zēngzǐ said:
"May I ask whether it is possible to be considered wise without wasting or being burdened?"
Kǒngzǐ became stern and raised his eyebrows, saying:
"Shēn,
do you consider a wise ruler to be burdened?
In the past, Shùn had Yǔ on his left and Gāoyáo on his right,
and without leaving his seat, the world was governed.
If the administration is not correct,
it is the fault of the ruler;
if the administration is correct,
but orders are not carried out,
it is the fault of those in charge of their duties.
Why would a wise ruler be burdened?
In the past, wise rulers inspected the borders without levying taxes,
visited markets without collecting duties,
taxed at a rate of one-tenth,
To employ the strength of the people,
[it] should not exceed three days per year;
entering the mountains and marshes should be done according to the seasons,
with prohibitions but without levies.
These six things
are ways to acquire wealth.
An enlightened ruler abandons four of these and moderates the other two;
how then does an enlightened ruler obtain his expenses?"
Zēng Zǐ said:
"May I venture to ask what are the Seven Instructions?"
Kǒng Zǐ said:
"If those above respect the elderly, then those below will become more filial;
if those above follow seniority, then those below will become more fraternal;
if those above enjoy giving, then those below will become more trustworthy;
if those above are close to the virtuous, then those below will choose their friends carefully;
if those above love virtue, then those below will not conceal [their faults];
if those above hate greed, then those below will be ashamed to contend;
if those above are steadfast and resolute, then those below will value integrity and honor;
when the people all have distinctions [of rank and duty],
then [they will be] upright and correct.
[This] is also not laborious.
This is called the Seven Instructions.
The Seven Instructions
are the foundation for governing the people;
when the instructions are settled, then things are rectified.
Those above
are the models for the people;
if the models are correct, then what thing will not be correct?
Therefore, if the ruler first establishes himself in benevolence,
then the senior officials will be loyal and the scholars trustworthy,
the common people will be honest,
the artisans simple,
the merchants sincere,
the young women innocent,
and the married women unassuming.
These seven
are the aims of education.
When these seven are spread throughout the world, they will not be excessive;
when confined to ordinary rooms, they will not be obstructed.
Therefore, the sage equalizes them with ritual,
establishes them with righteousness,
and carries them out with obedience,
and the people will cast off evil as if by washing."
Zēngzǐ said:
"Your disciple is not up to it,
but the principle is perfect."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Shēn,
let us stop there;
there is more.
In the past, enlightened rulers had methods for governing the people;
they necessarily divided the land into provinces,
assigning them to different jurisdictions for governance.
In this way, virtuous people had nowhere to hide,
and violent people had nowhere to conceal themselves.
They made officials examine the people daily,
If you examine them regularly,
and yearly encourage the virtuous,
then the virtuous will become close,
and the unworthy will be fearful.
Cause them to care for widowers and widows,
care for orphans and the solitary,
relieve the poor and impoverished,
encourage filial piety and brotherly respect,
and select the wise and promote the able.
If these seven things are cultivated,
then within the four seas,
there will be no people subject to punishment.
If those above treat those below as intimately as their own heart and belly,
then those below will treat those above as fondly as a child seeing its loving mother.
When those above and those below are so close to each other,
then orders will be followed,
and policies will be implemented.
Because the people who are already near are pleased,
those who are far away will come and submit.
Then, by spreading your fingers you will know an inch,
by spreading your hand you will know a foot,
by extending your elbow you will know a fathom,
ten fathoms make a cable's length.
One hundred paces make a wall,
three hundred paces make a *lǐ*,
one thousand paces make a well,
three wells make a *gōuliè*,
three *gōuliè* make a *jù*,
If fiefs are established every fifty *lǐ*,
and cities are established every hundred *lǐ*,
then provisions of clothing and furs will be stored.
This makes those who reside secure,
and those who travel have [a sense of] rise and fall [security when travelling].
Therefore, the *Mányí* barbarians and the various *Xià* peoples,
though their clothing and language are different,
none fail to come
to have an audience with the king.
Therefore it is said:
Even without markets, the people will not lack;
even without punishments, the people will not disobey.
The gains from netting birds, hunting, and tilling
are not used to fill the palaces;
what is collected from the people
is not used to fill the storehouses.
Extravagance is curbed to compensate for what is insufficient,
and rituals are used to reduce what is superfluous.
Therefore it is said:
With much sincerity and little outward appearance,
its rites can be preserved,
its trustworthiness can be relied upon,
and its traces can be followed.
Its trustworthiness
is like the four seasons of spring, autumn, winter, and summer;
its embrace of the myriad people
is like eating when hungry, drinking when thirsty.
The people of the lower lands trust in this!
The heat of summer and the cold of winter,
though far away, are brought near.
It is not that the Way is near,
but that its shining virtue extends.
Therefore, without moving armies, one inspires awe;
without dispensing benefits, one gains affection.
This is what is meant by the vigilance of an enlightened ruler.
"To parry attacks a thousand *lǐ* away,
this is what it refers to."
Zēngzǐ said:
"May I venture to ask what are the Three Perfections (sān zhì)?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Perfect propriety needs no yielding, yet the world is well-governed;
perfect rewards need no expenditure, yet the scholars of the world are pleased;
perfect music is without sound, yet the people of the world are in harmony.
An enlightened ruler earnestly practices the Three Perfections;
therefore, the rulers of the world can be known,
the scholars of the world can be made his ministers,
and the people of the world can be employed."
Zēngzǐ said:
"May I venture to ask what they are?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"In ancient times, enlightened rulers exhausted their knowledge of the names of the world's worthy scholars.
Having known their names,
they also knew their numbers;
having known their numbers,
they also knew their locations.
Enlightened rulers used the ranks of the world to honor the scholars of the world;
This is called the ultimate propriety: not yielding, yet the world is governed.
Distributing the wealth of the world,
to enrich the scholars of the world,
this is called the ultimate reward: not wasteful, yet the scholars of the world are pleased.
When the scholars of the world are pleased,
then the brilliant reputation of the world will flourish;
this is called the ultimate joy: without sound, yet the people of the world are harmonious.
Therefore it is said:
the so-called ultimate benevolence in the world
is the ability to unite those who are most closely related in the world;
the so-called ultimate wisdom in the world
is the ability to employ those who are most harmonious in the world;
the so-called ultimate discernment in the world
is the ability to select those who are most virtuous in the world.
When these three are all interconnected,
then one can undertake a campaign.
Therefore, for the benevolent, there is nothing greater than loving others;
for the wise, there is nothing greater than knowing the worthy;
for the ruler, there is nothing greater than employing the worthy.
If the ruler of a state cultivates these three,
then all within the four seas will respectfully watch,
and then he can undertake a campaign.
What an enlightened ruler attacks
must be where the Way is abandoned.
If they abandon the Way and do not practice it,
then punish their ruler,
carry out the campaign,
comfort their people, and do not seize their wealth.
Therefore, it is said:
The expeditions of an enlightened ruler
are like timely rain,
arriving to the joy of the people.
Therefore, his bestowals are exceedingly widespread,
and he gains the affection of exceedingly many.
This is what is meant by “returning with the army from upon the mat and seat."」
*Da Dai Li - Wu Di De* Zǎi Wǒ asked Kǒngzǐ, saying:
"In the past, I heard from Róng Yīlìng
that the Huángdì reigned for three hundred years.
May I ask, was the Huángdì a human,
or not a human?
How did he reach three hundred years?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Yǔ,
Tāng, Wén, Wǔ, Chéng Wáng, Zhōu Gōng—
can they be observed exhaustively?
As for the Huángdì, he is too remote.
What do you take him to be?
The masters of old rarely spoke of him."
Zǎi Wǒ said:
"The transmissions of ancient times,
obscure and subtle sayings,
fully debated distinctions,
and careless intentions,
are not the way of a gentleman.
Therefore, my question is certainly well-founded."
Kǒngzǐ said:
The Yellow Emperor,
was the son of Shǎo Diǎn,
named Xuān Yuán.
He was born with a divine spirit,
able to speak when young,
intelligent from childhood,
earnest and quick-witted when grown,
and discerning upon adulthood.
He governed the five qì,
established the five measures,
comforted the myriad people,
measured the four directions,
and taught the bears, *bā*, *pí*, leopards, and tigers,
to fight the Red Emperor in the wilderness of Bǎn Quán.
After three battles,
he was then able to achieve his ambition.
The Yellow Emperor wore an embroidered coat and skirt,
a large belt,
and an embroidered skirt,
riding a dragon and leaning on a cloud-patterned screen,
to conform to the principles of Heaven and Earth,
the reasons for darkness and light,
the explanations of life and death,
and the difficulties of survival and destruction.
He sowed the various grains, grasses, and trees in season,
therefore, his teachings transformed birds, beasts, insects, and other creatures,
observed the movements of the sun, moon, and stars,
and thoroughly exploited the earth, stones, metals, and jades.
Exerting his mind, strength, ears, and eyes,
He conserved water, fire, materials, and resources.
While alive, the people benefited from him for a hundred years;
After his death, the people feared his spirit for a hundred years;
After his passing, the people applied his teachings for a hundred years.
Therefore, it is said, "three hundred years."
Zǎi Wǒ asked about Emperor Zhuānxū.
Confucius said:
"The Five Emperors relied on explanations,
The Three Kings relied on measurements and standards.
You want to understand and distinguish the sayings of the ancient past in one day?
How rash you are, Yǔ!"
Zǎi Wǒ said:
"In the past, I heard from you, Master, that:
'The young ones should have no lingering questions.'"
Confucius said:
"Zhuānxū
was the grandson of the Yellow Emperor,
and the son of Chāngyì;
He was called Gāoyáng.
With deep and profound wisdom, he possessed strategies;
He was clear and thorough, and understood matters;
He nurtured resources to suit the land;
He followed the seasons to emulate Heaven;
He relied on ghosts and spirits to establish righteousness;
He regulated the Qi to instruct the people;
He used purity and sincerity in sacrifices.
Riding dragons, he reached the four seas,
Reaching north to Yōulíng,
south to Jiāozhǐ,
west crossing the moving sands,
and east to Pánmù.
Moving and still things,
great and small spirits,
all that the sun and moon illuminate,
none fail to be reverent and diligent."
Zǎi Wǒ said:
"May I ask about Dì Kù?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"He was the grandson of Yuán Xiāo,
the son of Tǎn Jí,
named Gāo Xīn.
Born divine and spiritual,
he named himself.
He generously bestowed benefits on all things,
not for his own sake.
With his intelligence, he knew what was distant;
with his clarity, he observed what was subtle.
He followed the righteousness of Heaven
and understood the people's needs.
He was benevolent yet authoritative,
kind yet trustworthy.
He cultivated himself, and the world submitted.
He took the wealth of the land but used it sparingly.
He nurtured and taught the myriad people and profited them with instruction.
He calculated the days and months to welcome and send them off.
He clarified the spirits and gods and respectfully served them.
His countenance was dignified,
his virtue lofty.
His actions were timely,
his attire befitting a scholar.
In spring and summer, he rode dragons;
in autumn and winter, he rode horses.
He wore yellow fǔ and fú robes,
maintained the middle way, and thus gained the empire.
Wherever the sun and moon shone,
wherever wind and rain reached,
none failed to follow and obey him."
Zǎi Wǒ said:
"May I ask about Dì Yáo?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"He was the son of Gāo Xīn,
named Fàng Xūn.
His benevolence was like Heaven,
his wisdom like the spirits.
Approaching him was like approaching the sun,
beholding him was like beholding the clouds.
He was wealthy but not arrogant,
noble but not haughty.
He wore yellow fǔ and fú robes,
rode in a red carriage with white horses.
Bó Yí presided over the rites,
Lóng and Kuí taught dancing.
He promoted Shùn and Péng Zǔ and entrusted them with responsibilities.
The Xiānmín (先民, Former Sages) governed them according to the four seasons.
He exiled Gònggōng (共工) to Yōuzhōu (幽州),
in order to transform the Northern Dí (北狄, Northern Barbarians);
banished Dōu (兜) to Chóngshān (崇山),
in order to transform the Southern Mán (南蠻, Southern Barbarians);
executed Sāmiáo (三苗) at Sānwēi (三危),
in order to transform the Western Róng (西戎, Western Barbarians);
and executed Gǔn (鯀) at Yǔshān (羽山),
in order to transform the Eastern Yí (東夷, Eastern Barbarians).
His words were consistent,
his virtue did not deviate.
Within the four seas,
wherever boats and carriages reached,
none did not rejoice in his governance."
Zǎi Wǒ (宰我) said:
"May I ask about Emperor Shùn (舜)?"
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"He was the grandson of Jiǎo Niú (蟜牛),
the son of Gǔ Sǒu (瞽叟),
named Chóng Huá (重華).
He loved learning and was filial and fraternal,
known throughout the four seas.
As a potter, he served his parents,
with generosity, gentleness, kindness, and goodness.
He taught with sincerity and knew the times,
he feared Heaven and loved the people,
he cared for those far away and was close to his relatives.
He received the great mandate,
Relying on Ní Huáng,
wise, insightful, and understanding,
he became the king of the world.
He sent Yǔ to survey the land,
to oversee the famous mountains and rivers,
in order to benefit the people.
He sent Hòu Jì to sow seeds,
diligently cultivating fine grains,
in order to provide food and drink.
Xī Hé oversaw the calendar,
respectfully instructing the people about the seasons.
He sent Yì to manage fire,
in order to clear the mountains and scrubland.
Bó Yí was in charge of ritual,
in order to regulate the world.
Kuí created music,
to sing and dance with appeals,
harmonized with bells and drums.
Gāo Yáo was in charge of law,
loyal, trustworthy, and clear in judgment,
understanding the feelings of the people.
Qì served as Minister of Education,
teaching the people filial piety and fraternity,
respecting governance and following the classics.
His words were not deceptive,
his virtue was not concealed,
he promoted the virtuous and the world was at peace.
To the south he pacified Jiāo Zhǐ,
He greatly set free the Xiānzhī, Qúsōu, Dī, and Qiāng peoples,
as well as the Běishān, Róng, Fā, and Xīshèn peoples,
and to the east, the Cháng and Niǎoyí Yǔmín peoples.
When Shùn was young,
he suffered hardship and toil.
At twenty, he was known throughout the world for his filial piety.
At thirty, he was in position.
He succeeded to the imperial throne.
He died at fifty
and was buried in the wilds of Cāngwú."
Zǎi Wǒ said:
"May I ask about Yǔ?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"He was the grandson of Gāoyáng
and the son of Gǔn,
and was called Wénmìng.
He was quick, clever, and capable of accomplishment.
His virtue did not falter.
His benevolence was approachable.
His words were trustworthy.
His voice set the standard for musical pitch,
his person set the standard for measurement.
He was praised as the best of officials.
He was diligent and reverent,
serving as the guiding principle and organizational framework.
He toured the nine provinces,
opened up the nine roads,
managed the nine marshes,
He measured the nine mountains.
He acted as the master of the spirits,
and as the father and mother of the people.
On his left, he held the plumb line and level;
on his right, the compass and square.
He traversed the four seasons,
and governed the four seas.
He pacified the nine provinces,
and upheld the nine heavens.
He clarified sight and hearing,
and governed the world.
He promoted Gāo Yáo and Yì to assist him,
and he raised weapons to punish those unoffering, unprincipled, and immoral people.
Within the four seas,
wherever ships and carriages reached,
all submitted."
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Yǔ,
his greatness is as described;
the people rejoiced to the utmost.
I am not the man for such a task."
Zǎi Wǒ said,
"I am not trustworthy enough,
but I respectfully accept the charge."
Another day,
Zǎi Wǒ told this to others.
Someone repeated this at the place where the gentlemen studied,
Kǒngzǐ said,
"If I wanted to judge people by their appearance, I
would change it because of Miè Míng (滅明);
if I wanted to judge people by their words, I
would change it because of Yǔ (予);
if I wanted to judge people by their countenance, I
would change it because of Shī (師)."
Zǎi Wǒ (宰我) heard this and was afraid,
and did not dare to appear.
*Dà Dài Lǐ · Yú Dài Dé* (《大戴禮·虞戴德》) The Duke said:

Where did he derive his lofty actions from?"
Confucius said:
"You ask me about it,
but I, Qiū (丘), have nothing further to add.
Your understanding seems incomplete;
the Yellow Emperor (Huángdì, 黃帝) admired and cultivated it." He said:
"He illuminated the laws according to Heaven,
and clearly initiated teaching for the people.
Practicing this,
one can achieve a superior understanding of Heaven's transformative power.
Things will certainly arise,
therefore the people are ordered and do not change."
The Duke said:
"Excellent!
To teach the people according to Heaven,

Confucius said:
"Acceptable.
Although acceptable, yet not followed,

The relationship of father to son

the relationship of ruler to subject

For a son not to serve his father,
for a subject not to serve his ruler,
is this not rebelling against Heaven and acting perversely?
Therefore, for a son not to serve his father

for a subject not to serve his ruler,
he will surely be executed.
Following Heaven, punishments are created;
from Earth, myriad things are produced.

revere Heaven and emulate Earth;
being able to employ the virtue of the people,

they valued knowledge and loved benevolence,

When these three constant rituals are clear, one's reputation will not be flawed.

Therefore, in high antiquity, there were no taboos;
they rectified the names of Heaven.
The palace of the Son of Heaven has four connecting passages,

The Son of Heaven uses a jade tablet,

To combine these three and enact them as one,

The Son of Heaven announces the first day of the month to the feudal lords,

Therefore, failure to arrive will certainly be punished.
When feudal lords meet each other,
a qing serves as an envoy,

The Son of Heaven, in the second month of the year, builds an altar in the eastern suburbs,
erecting five-colored banners,
displaying the five weapons,
preparing the five flavors,

and listening to clear instructions.
Positioning targets,
Kàngdà hóu,
guī hú,
jiān wù.

When the feudal lords instruct their officers,
the officers, holding bows and arrows,

With upright minds and proper appearances,

When the world follows the Way,

When a state follows the Way,

When a family is not in chaos,

Therefore, when the sage instructs the people,

Matters of Heaven are called clarity (míng),

Foolish people are called traitors;
traitors must be punished.
Therefore, the world is at peace and the state is well-governed,

Living in small communities, they are not restrained;

in small numbers, they are confused.

going on expeditions, they conquer.
This is the supreme virtue of officials and people."
The Duke said,

The Duke said,

What was raised up, they suppressed;
what was suppressed, they raised up;
they connected them with virtuous conduct,

The duke said,

create the blessings of Earth,

The Duke said:
"Excellent!" *Dà Dài Lǐ·Gào Zhì*
The Duke said:

the offering of millet must be pure,

The Master said:
"Qiū does not know if it can reduce resentment."
The Duke said:

The Master said:
"Gather people with rites according to the seasons.
When the people see these rites, those above and below will support each other.
If they support each other, they will be joyful.
If they are joyful, then they will have no worries.
In this way, resentment will be reduced and disorder will not arise.
The rites
should accord with the four seasons,
the first month of each season, the last month of each season, the five domestic animals, and the five grains.
Ensuring that everything arrives at the right time, according to its season.
I, Qiū, do not yet know if this can avert disaster from afar."
The Duke said:
"Then what is the purpose of doing this?"
The Master said:
"When wisdom and benevolence are combined, then Heaven and Earth are complete.
When Heaven and Earth are complete, then all things are in season.
When all things are in season, then the people are respectful of wealth.
When the people are respectful of wealth, they work according to the seasons.
Working according to the seasons moderates affairs.
Moderating affairs allows one to mobilize the masses.
Mobilizing the masses requires a standard.
When a standard is used to employ the people, they are encouraged.
When they are encouraged, they achieve results.
When they achieve results, there is no resentment.
When there is no resentment, the succession lasts long,
only for the Sage.
Therefore, government aims to benefit the masses,
not to oppress them;
The multitude are [employed] to accomplish successful matters,
not to deal with detrimental matters.
Matters are [managed] to pacify the people,
not to exploit the people.
Therefore, having vast lands and a large populace
should not be used as a source of wealth for prolonging disasters.
Qiū (丘) [Confucius] heard the Grand Historian of Zhōu (周) say:
If governance does not follow Heaven,
and the people do not follow [the ruler],
then all things are easily ruined and difficult to achieve.
Yú Shǐ Bó Yí (虞史伯夷) said: "Míng (明)" [brightness]
means "mèng (孟)" [beginning].
"Yōu (幽)" [darkness] means "yòu (幼)" [end].
"Míng yōu (明幽)" [brightness and darkness]
are like the female and the male.
The alternating rise of the female and the male is harmonious,
and it is the standard of utmost righteousness.
The sun returns to the west,
and brightness arises in the east.
The moon returns to the east,
and brightness arises in the west.
The calendar of the Yú (虞) and Xià (夏) dynasties
correctly begins in the first month of spring.

in accordance with the four seasons,
He died on the winter solstice.
At that time, the cock crowed three times,
and then it became bright.
He was carried in a blue-colored (coffin),
according to the twelve months' seasonal observances,
and died in the Chǒu hour (1-3 AM).
The sun and moon complete the annual calendar,
with an intercalary month every other year to accord with the way of Heaven;
this is called the "Suì Yú Zhī Yuè" (Year of Abundance Month).
Heaven's way is called "zuò míng" (to make bright),
called "yǔ" (to grant),
thereby Heaven accomplishes its task;
Earth's way is called "zuò chāng" (to make flourish),
called "yǔ" (to grant),
thereby Earth accomplishes its work;
Humanity's way is called "zuò lè" (to make joyful),
called "yǔ" (to grant),
thereby the people are happy.
The people's active abilities
are never far from their tasks;
the people's sorrowful expressions
are never far from their virtue;
this is called a harmonious combination of inner and outer qualities.
The way in which things are produced,
and the way of flourishing and prosperity are thus.
Heaven produces things,
Earth nourishes things,
things are fully prepared and thrive, and time is used according to constant principles;
They are called sages;
The one who presides over sacrifices to Heaven,
Is called the Son of Heaven (Tiānzǐ).
When the Son of Heaven passes away,
He is measured by paces on the Sìchuān River,
And represented by the four mountains;
His final burial is called "Emperor" (Dì).
Heaven creates benevolence,
Earth creates wealth,
Man creates governance;
To delight in governance without weariness,
And to regulate wealth according to the seasons,
Therefore, when sages succeed, there is good governance.
King Wén governed while awaiting the opportune time,
Tāng governed to subdue chaos,
Yǔ governed by relocating the masses.
The masses were convinced,
And with this, he established the world (天下 tiānxià).
Yáo valued delighting in governing at the right time,
And recommended Shùn.
Shùn governed by employing strength through virtue.
Governing the people in the state was like practicing forbearance (恕 shù),
Nurturing officials at home, and thereby governing the state.
Pacify them without changing,
Encourage them without discouraging,
And the people will all abandon evil as if advancing towards goodness.
The ruler induces goodness and implements punishments,
The common people will exhaust themselves in benevolence and achieve peace;
This is the way ancient wise rulers governed the world.
The benevolent were considered sages,
the noble were next in importance,
the strong were next,
the beautiful were next,
and those skilled in archery and chariot driving were next.
Those who governed the world in ancient times were certainly sages.
If a sage possessed a state,
then the sun and moon would not be eclipsed,
the stars would not fall,
the Bóhǎi Sea would not shift,
the Yellow River would not overflow,
the rivers and marshes would not dry up,
the mountains would not collapse,
the hills would not yield grain inappropriately,
the bathing rivers would not be deserted,
and the deep pools would not run dry.
At that time, dragons would arrive and not be hidden,
phoenixes would descend and forget to flap their wings,

birds of prey would forget to use their talons,
bees and scorpions would not sting infants,
mosquitoes and gadflies would not bite celestial foals,
the Lùo River would produce auspicious omens,
and the Yellow River would produce charts.
From the earliest times until now,
nothing has surpassed benevolence.
The prosperity of a state,
When a state is good,
it trusts in benevolence.
Therefore, without rewards or punishments,
it is as if the people all exert their strength,
carts do not erect spears,
those near and far are all submissive,
sincerity causes envoys to come and go,
foreign guests all arrive,
without resentment or hatred,
all follow virtuous conduct.
This is without empty ceremonies,
without empty reputations.
Worthy people share common worries,
cruel harms are inspected in a timely manner,
those who are good are promoted as good,
those who are virtuous are promoted as virtuous,

The Master said,

Tāng took men based on their reputation (rén yǐ shēng);

The Duke said,

The Duke was afraid and said:

*Hán Shī Wàizhuàn* 5 Confucius was sitting in attendance on Jì Sūn (the head of the Ji family).
Jì Sūn's steward Tōng (said):
"The lord has people borrow horses,
should he give them?"
Confucius said:
"I have heard that when a lord takes from his ministers,
it is called 'taking,'
and not 'borrowing.'"
Jìsūn Wù,
told his steward Tōng,
"From now on,
if the lord takes something, call it 'taking,'
do not say 'borrowing.'"
*Han Shi Waizhuan* 7 Confucius said:
"In the past,
the Duke of Zhōu served King Wén,
his actions were without independent decisions,
his affairs were not based on his own will,
his body appeared as if it could not bear the weight of his clothes,
his words seemed as if they would not leave his mouth,
carrying and holding things in front of him,
cautiously as if he were about to lose them,
he can be called a son.
When King Wǔ died,
King Chéng was young,
the Duke of Zhōu inherited the undertakings of Wén and Wǔ,
occupied the position of the Son of Heaven,
listened to the government of the Son of Heaven,
campaigned against the rebellions of the Ī Dí barbarians,
punished the crimes of Guǎn and Cài,
held King Chéng and faced the feudal lords in court,
deciding on punishments and rewards with resolute judgment,
without consulting anyone,
his authority moved Heaven and Earth,
shaking and frightening within the seas,
he can be called capable of martial prowess.
When Chéng Wáng grew up,
the Duke of Zhōu returned the government,
faced north and served him,
acting only after seeking permission,
showing no boastful or arrogant expression.
He can be called a true subject.
Therefore, the reason why one person
can adapt three times
is to respond to the times."

Confucius said,

men."

"Knowing the worthy is wisdom;
to know the worthy is wisdom,

Having these three,

*Shuō Yuàn · Chén Shù* Zǐ Gòng asked Kǒngzǐ,
"Among the ministers of today,
who are the worthy ones?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"I do not know.
In the past, Qí had Bào Shū,
Zhèng had Zǐ Pí,
they were worthy men."
Zǐ Gòng said,
"Then did Qí not have Guǎn Zhòng and Zhèng not have Zǐ Chǎn?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Cì,
you only know one thing and not the other.
Have you heard of recommending the worthy as being worthy?
Or exerting effort as being worthy?"
Zǐ Gòng said,
"Recommending the worthy as being worthy."
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Yes, I have heard of Bào Shū recommending Guǎn Zhòng,
and heard of Zǐ Pí recommending Zǐ Chǎn,
but I have not heard of Guǎn Zhòng or Zǐ Chǎn recommending anyone."
*Liú Zǐ · Jiàn Xián* In the past,
Zǐ Gòng asked Kǒngzǐ,
"Who are the great worthies?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Qí had Bào Shū, Zhèng had Zǐ Pí."
Zǐgòng said:
"Does Qí lack Guǎn Zhòng, and Zhèng lack Zǐchǎn?"
The Master said:
"I have heard of promoting the worthy as worthy,
and regarding the unworthy as unworthy.
Bào Shū recommended Guǎn Zhòng,
Zǐpí recommended Zǐchǎn.

*Yànzi Chūnqiū · Jiàn Xià*: Yànzi was on a diplomatic mission to Lǔ.
Before he returned,
Duke Jǐng ordered the people of the state to begin the great platform project.
The cold of the year did not cease,
and there were those in the villages who were freezing and starving.
The people of the state looked to Yànzi.
Yànzi arrived,
and resumed his duties.
The Duke then sat down
and enjoyed drinking and music.
Yànzi said:
"If Your Lordship would grant me a favor,
I request to sing a song."
He sang:
"The common people say:
'The freezing water washes over me,
what shall I do!
The great roof does not shelter me,
what shall I do!'"
When the song ended,
With a sigh, he lamented and shed tears.
The Duke went and stopped him, saying:
"Why has Master come to this?
It must be because of the laborers on the Dàtái project!
I will quickly halt it."
Yàn Zǐ bowed twice.
He went out without a word,
and then went to Dàtái,
holding a simple whip and striking those who were not working diligently, saying:
"We common people
all have covered huts
to avoid dryness and dampness.
The Duke is building a platform, yet it is not being completed quickly,
why is this?"
The people all said:
"Yàn Zǐ is helping Heaven to be tyrannical."
Yàn Zǐ returned.
Before he arrived,
the Duke issued an order to hasten the end of the labor,
chariots raced and people hurried.
Zhòng Ní heard of this
and sighed, saying:
"The good ministers of old
attributed fame and reputation to their ruler
and calamities to themselves.
When in court, they earnestly corrected their ruler's wrongdoings;
when out of court, they highly praised their ruler's virtue and righteousness.
Therefore, even when serving a lazy ruler,
He was able to wear his robes and
hold court with the various lords,
yet they did not dare diminish his merit.
"The one who embodies this principle,
isn't it Yàn Zǐ!"
*Yàn Zǐ Chūnqiū · Wèn Xià* Liángqiū Jù asked Yàn Zǐ,
"You serve three rulers,
but the rulers' hearts are not the same,
and you comply with them all.
Does a benevolent person truly have many hearts?"
Yàn Zǐ replied,
"I have heard that
consistent and unflagging love
can be used to guide the common people;
the violent and disloyal
cannot be used to guide even one person.
One heart can be used to serve a hundred rulers,
but three hearts cannot be used to serve one ruler."
Zhòngní heard this and said,
"Young men, remember this!
Yàn Zǐ is one who serves a hundred rulers with one heart."
*Yàn Zǐ Chūnqiū · Zá Shàng* Yàn Zǐ was sent to Lǔ,
Zhòngní sent his disciples to observe him.
Zǐgòng returned
and reported,
"Who said that Yàn Zǐ is versed in ritual?
For the rites say:
'When ascending the stairs, do not step on the same place twice;
"One does not hasten on the dais,
one does not kneel when receiving jade."
Now, Yàn Zǐ does the opposite of all this;
who would say Yàn Zǐ is versed in ritual?"
Yàn Zǐ having completed his business with the ruler of Lǔ,
withdrew and met with Zhòng Ní.
Zhòng Ní said,
"According to ritual,
one does not skip steps when ascending,
one does not hasten on the dais,
one does not kneel when receiving jade.
Did you do the opposite of this?"
Yàn Zǐ said,
"Yīng has heard that between the two pillars,
the ruler and subject have their positions;
the ruler performs one (act),
the subject performs two.
The ruler's arrival was swift,
therefore I skipped steps ascending the dais and hastened to my position.
The ruler humbly presented the jade,
so I knelt to receive it.
Moreover, I have heard that
for important matters, one does not overstep boundaries,
for minor matters, entering and exiting is permissible."
Yàn Zǐ departed,
Zhòng Ní saw him off with the courtesy due a guest,
disregarding the usual considerations.
Only Yàn Zǐ was able to perform this.
Han Shi Waizhuan, Book 4: Yàn Zǐ's Mission to Lǔ,
Upon ascending the hall, he hastened;

Yàn Zǐ heard of this,

A disciple of Mìngmén said:
"He saves the people without boasting,

Yàn Zǐ is truly a gentleman."

*Hánfēizǐ · Wàichǔ Shuō Yòuxià*. The lord of Wèi entered the court of Zhōu.

*Hán Fēi Zǐ · Nán Yī* Xiāng Zǐ was besieged in Jìnyáng.
After escaping the siege,
he rewarded five people who had contributed.
Gāo Hè was the first to be rewarded.
Zhāng Mèngtán said:
"In the matter of Jìnyáng,
Hè had no great merit,
yet now he is the first to be rewarded,

Xiāng Zǐ said:
"In the matter of Jìnyáng,
my state was in danger, and my altars of state were nearly lost.
None of my ministers did not have an intention of arrogance and disrespect,
only Hè Zǐ did not lose the proper etiquette between ruler and subject,
therefore he is placed first."
Zhòng Ní heard of it and said:
"What an excellent reward!
Xiāng Zǐ rewards one person,
and all under heaven who are ministers dare not be disrespectful."
*Lǚshì Chūnqiū · Xiàoxíng Lǎn · Yì Shǎng* Zhào Xiāng Zǐ escaped the siege,
and rewarded five people who had contributed,
Gāo Hè was the first.

"Within Jìnyáng,
Hè had no great merit.
To reward him and place him first,

Xiāng Zǐ said:
"My state was in danger, the altars of state were precarious,

Among those who associated with me and did not fail in the proper rites between lord and minister,

This is why I put him first."
Zhòngní heard of this and said:
"Xiāng Zǐ can be said to be good at rewarding!
By rewarding one person,
all the ministers in the world will dare not fail in proper rites."

Only Hè.
