"Lǚshì Chūnqiū · Mèngchūn Jì · Qù Sī" Duke Píng of Jìn asked Qí Huángyáng, saying:
"There is no magistrate in Nányáng.
Who is suitable to be appointed?"
Qí Huángyáng replied, saying:
"Xiè Hú is suitable."
Duke Píng said:
"Is Xiè Hú not your enemy?"
He replied:
"Your Lordship asked who is suitable,
not who is my enemy."
Duke Píng said:
"Good."
Thereupon he employed him,
and the people of the state praised it as good.
After some time,
Duke Píng again asked Qí Huángyáng, saying:
"There is no commandant in the state.
Who is suitable to be appointed?"
He replied, saying:
"Wǔ Kě is acceptable."
Píng Gōng said,
"Is Wǔ not your son?"
He replied,
"You asked about acceptability,
not about my son."
Píng Gōng said,
"Good."
He then employed him,
and the people of the state praised his decision.
Kǒngzǐ heard of this and said,
"Excellent!
Qí Huángyáng's judgment!
In recommending from outside, he did not avoid his enemy;
in recommending from within, he did not avoid his son.
Qí Huángyáng can be called impartial!"
*Lǚshì Chūnqiū · Bù Gǒu Lùn* When Wǔ Wáng arrived at the outskirts of Yīn,
his sash became untied.
Five men stood before him,
but none were willing to tie it for him, saying,
"The reason we serve our lord
is not for tying sashes."
Wǔ Wáng released the white feather from his left hand
and the yellow axe from his right hand,
and exerted himself to tie it himself.
Kǒngzǐ heard of this and said,
"These five men
are the kind who can assist a king,
"This is what an unworthy ruler cannot be secure with."
Therefore, even the Son of Heaven may not be able to overcome the common people,
and the empire may not be able to overcome a state possessing a thousand chariots.
*Lǚshì Chūnqiū·Shì Róng Lùn·Wù Dà* Confucius said:
"Swallows and sparrows compete for good places under one roof,
mothers and children feeding each other,
contentedly enjoying themselves,
thinking themselves safe.
When the chimney collapses,
and the upper beams burn,
the swallows' and sparrows' expressions do not change.
Why is this?
They do not know that disaster is about to befall them,
are they not foolish!
Those who are ministers and are no more intelligent than swallows and sparrows
are few!"
*Yántiě Lùn·Tōng Yǒu* Formerly, when Sūn Shū'áo was prime minister of Chǔ,
his wife did not wear silk,
and his horses were not fed grain.
Confucius said:
"This is not permissible.
Extreme frugality at the top
is what crickets do."
*Yántiě Lùn·Bāo Xián* The power of the Jì and Mèng families,
the wealth of the Three Huán families,
cannot be attained.
Confucius said of them:
"If he is not a minister,
Those whose power equals the ruler's and whose wealth matches the state's will perish!"
*Shuō Yuàn · Chén Shù* (Garden of Stories · The Art of the Minister) Jiǎn Zǐ had ministers Yǐn Chuò and Shè Jué.
Jiǎn Zǐ said:
"Jué loves me.
When he remonstrates with me, he never does so in front of others.
Chuò, on the other hand,
does not love me;
when he remonstrates with me, he always does so in front of others."
Yǐn Chuò said:
"Jué
loves the ruler's shame
but does not love the ruler's faults.
A minister should love the ruler's faults
and not love the ruler's shame."
Confucius said:
"What a virtuous man is Yǐn Chuò!
He criticizes without praising."
*Shuō Yuàn · Fù Ēn* (Garden of Stories · Repaying Kindness) Confucius said:
"In the north, there is a beast
whose name is Jué.
Its front feet are like a rat's,
and its hind feet are like a rabbit's.
This beast,
greatly loves the qióngqióng and the jùxū.
When it finds sweet grass,
it always gnaws off some to give to the qióngqióng and the jùxū.
When the qióngqióng and the jùxū see people coming,
they always carry Jué away.
Jué (蹶) does not inherently love Qióngqióng (蛩蛩) and Jùxū (巨虛),
but does so because they lend it their feet.
These two beasts,
likewise do not inherently love Jué (蹷),
but do so because it finds sweet grass and leaves it for them.
Even birds, beasts, and insects
know to rely on borrowing and mutually repay each other.
How much more so should gentlemen who desire to establish fame and fortune in the world?"
Jiè Zǐtuī (介子推) was only fifteen when he became chancellor of Jīng (荊).
Zhòng Ní (仲尼) heard of this
and sent someone to observe. Upon their return, they said,
"In the corridor, there are twenty-five talented men,
and in the hall, there are twenty-five elders."
Zhòng Ní (仲尼) said,
"Combining the wisdom of these twenty-five men,
they are wiser than Tāng (湯) and Wǔ (武).
Combining the strength of these twenty-five men,
they are stronger than Péng Zǔ (彭祖).
To govern the world with them,
its stability is assured!"
Confucius was sitting idly
and sighed deeply, saying,
"If only Tóngdī Bóhuá (銅鞮伯華) had not died,
the world would surely be settled!"
Zǐ Lù (子路) said,
"May I ask, what kind of person was he?"
Confucius said,
"In his youth,
Intelligent and fond of learning;
when he is strong,
he is courageous and unyielding;
when he is old,
he possesses principle and is able to be humble toward others.”
Zǐ Lù 子路 said:
“When he is young,
intelligent and fond of learning,
then that is acceptable;
when he is strong,
courageous and unyielding,
then that is acceptable;
if one possesses principle, then who would he be humble towards?”
Kǒngzǐ 孔子 said:
“Yóu 由 does not understand.
I have heard it said,
that when the many attack the few,
there is nothing that is not destroyed;
when the noble are humble towards the base,
there is nothing that is not obtained.
In the past, Zhōu Gōng Dàn 周公旦 established the policies of the empire,
and was humble towards seventy scholars.
Did he not possess principle?
He desired to obtain the services of scholars.
A man who possesses principle and is able to be humble towards the scholars of the world,
is a gentleman!”
*Shuō Yuàn* 說苑 · *Zhèng Jiàn* 正諫: There are five kinds of remonstrance:
First is direct remonstrance,
second is submissive remonstrance,
third is loyal remonstrance,
fourth is blunt remonstrance,
fifth is veiled remonstrance.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"I would follow veiled remonstrance!"
Now, not remonstrating endangers the ruler,
resolute remonstrance endangers oneself;
rather than endangering the ruler,
I would rather endanger myself.
If one endangers oneself and is still not heeded,
then the remonstrance is also without merit.
The wise assess the ruler's power and the timing,
adjust their urgency,
and act appropriately.
Above, they dare not endanger the ruler,
below, they do not endanger themselves.
Therefore, residing in the state, the state is not endangered;
residing in oneself, oneself is not imperiled.
*Báihǔ Tōng · Jiànzhēng* Kǒngzǐ said:
"There are five kinds of remonstrance,
I follow the way of veiled remonstrance.
Serving the ruler,
when advancing, think of exhausting loyalty,
when retreating, think of making up for faults,
when leaving, do not slander,
when remonstrating, do not expose."
*Shuō Yuàn · Zhèng Jiàn*: King Zhāo of Chǔ wanted to travel to the Jīng Terrace.
Sīmǎ Zǐqí stepped forward to advise, saying:
"The tour of the Jīng Terrace,
to the left is the waves of Lake Dòngtíng,
to the right is the water of Lake Pénglǐ,
to the south one looks upon Hunting Mountain,
below one overlooks the Fāng River.
Its pleasures cause people to forget old age and death.
When rulers tour such places,
they all end up losing their states.
I hope Your Majesty will not go there."
The king said:
"The Jīng Terrace is my land.
Having the land and touring it,
why do you forbid me from touring it?"
Angrily, he struck him.
Thereupon, Lìngyǐn Zǐxī drove a comfortable carriage pulled by four horses,
directly to the foot of the palace, saying:
"Today's tour of the Jīng Terrace,
cannot be missed."
The king boarded the carriage and patted his back, saying:
"The tour of the Jīng Terrace,
I will share its pleasures with you."
They rode ten *lǐ*,
then he pulled the reins and stopped, saying:
"Your servant dares not get out of the carriage.
I wish to have a way to speak;
is Your Majesty willing to listen to it?"
The king said,
"Tell me your reasons."
The *Lìngyǐn* Zǐxī said,
"I have heard that
a subject who is loyal to his ruler
cannot be sufficiently rewarded with titles and emoluments;
a subject who flatters his ruler
cannot be sufficiently punished with penalties.
Sīmǎ Zǐqí is
a loyal subject;
as for me,
I am a flattering subject.
I wish that Your Majesty would kill me,
punish my family,
and bestow rewards upon Sīmǎ Zǐqí."
The king said,
"If I were able to restrain my listening,
only you, *Gōngzǐ*, could prevent my excursion.
If later generations take up this excursion,
there would be no end to it.
What should be done?"
The *Lìngyǐn* Zǐxī said,
"It would be easy to prohibit later generations.
If Your Majesty's mountain mausoleum crumbles,
and you are entombed in the Jīngtái,
there has never been one who would hold bells, drums, pipes, and stringed instruments and make merry on his father's grave."
Thereupon, the king turned the chariot around,
and in the end did not tour the Jīngtái,
and ordered the previous arrangements to be canceled.
Kǒngzǐ, hearing of this from Lǔ, said,
"How admirable is the *Lìngyǐn* Zǐxī!
He remonstrated from ten *lǐ* away
and considered the matter for a hundred generations to come."
*Shuō Yuàn* · Miscellaneous Sayings. Qí Gāotíng asked Kǒngzǐ:
"Tíng does not neglect the mountains,
nor does he straighten the land,
he wears a straw raincoat,
and carries tools,
exhausting his energy to inquire about the way to serve a ruler.
I hope you, Master, will tell me."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Be upright and manage it,
be respectful and assist him,
treat people without weariness,
when you see a gentleman, then promote him,
when you see a petty person, then distance yourself from him,
remove your evil intentions,
and be loyal to him,
be quick in your actions,
cultivate your propriety,
even if thousands of *lǐ* away,
be as close as brothers.
If your actions are not quick,
and your propriety is not in accordance,
you will not be able to communicate even across the door."
*Bàopǔzi·Wàipiān·Yìmín*. Formerly, when Yán Huí died,
Dìnggōng of Lǔ was about to personally offer condolences,
and sent someone to inquire of Zhòng Ní.
Zhòng Ní said:
"All those within the state
are subjects."
Thereupon, Dìnggōng ascended
from the eastern steps,
performing the rites of a subject.
Zǐgòng said:
"Chén Línggōng and his ministers engaged in licentious behavior in the court.
Xiè Yě remonstrated and was killed.
He is the same as Bǐgān;
can he be called benevolent?"
Confucius said:
"Bǐgān, in relation to Zhòu,
was his uncle in kinship
and the Junior Tutor in office.
His loyal and sincere heart
was solely focused on preserving the ancestral temple.
Therefore, he contended with certain death,
hoping that after his death,
Zhòu would repent.
His fundamental intention lay in benevolence.
Xiè Yě's position was that of a junior grand master;
he had no kinship ties
but clung to favor and did not leave.
With his meager self,
he wished to correct the licentious darkness of an entire state.
To die without benefit
can be called regrettable.
The *Shī* (Book of Poetry) says:
"The people are very wayward,
do not establish for yourself a crooked path."
Is this not speaking of Xiè Yě?!”
*Jiāodào* 7
*Hán Shī Wàizhuàn* 9: Kǒngzǐ was traveling in the wilds of Shǎoyuán,
and there was a woman crying in the middle of the marsh,
her voice was very sad.
Kǒngzǐ found it strange
and sent a disciple to ask her, saying:
"Madam, why do you cry so sadly?"
The woman replied,
"Earlier,
while cutting *shī* firewood, I lost my *shī* hairpin,
and that is why I am sad."
The disciple said:
"Cutting *shī* firewood and losing a *shī* hairpin,
what is there to be sad about?"
The woman said:
"It is not the loss of the hairpin that I grieve,
but rather that I do not forget the past."
*Hán Shī Wàizhuàn* 9: Zǐlù said:
"If people treat me well,
I will also treat them well;
if people do not treat me well,
I will not treat them well."
Zǐgòng said:
"If people are good to me,
I will also be good to them;
if people are not good to me,
then I will just guide them to advance or retreat."
Yánhuí said:
"If people are good to me,
I will also be good to them;
if people are not good to me,
I will also be good to them."
The three disciples each held different views.
They asked the Master about it.
The Master said:
"What Yóu said
is the language of barbarians;
what Cì said
is the language of friends;
what Huí said
is the language of relatives."
*Han Shi Waizhuan* 10. Yānyuān asked Confucius, saying:
"I, Yuān, wish to be poor as if rich,
lowly as if noble,
without courage yet have authority,
associate with scholars,
and have no troubles or difficulties throughout my life;
would that be possible?"
Confucius said:
"Excellent, Huí!
To be poor yet seem rich
is due to knowing contentment and having no desires;
to be lowly yet seem noble
is due to yielding and having propriety;
to lack courage yet be imposing
is due to being respectful and not failing in one's dealings with others;
to have no troubles throughout one's life
is due to choosing one's words carefully before speaking them.
Someone like Huí
has reached this state!
Even the ancient sages
were only like this."
*Xúnzǐ*, "Kingcraft and Hegemony" Confucius said:
"Examine the means by which I treat others,
and the means by which others come to me."
*Xúnzǐ*, "Yáo Asked" Zǐgòng asked Confucius, saying:
"Cì acts as someone's subordinate, but doesn't understand it."
Confucius said:
"To be a subordinate
is like the earth!
Dig it deeply and you obtain sweet spring water;
plant in it and the five grains flourish;
grasses and trees grow;
birds and beasts are nurtured;
the living stand on it;
the dead enter it;
it accumulates its merits tirelessly.
To be a subordinate
It is like earth."
*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn*, Seven. Confucius was idly sitting,
Zǐgòng was attending upon him,
and asked, "What is the Way of being subordinate to others?
What should one do?"
Confucius said,
"Excellent!
This is a good question you ask.
To be subordinate to others,
it is like earth!"
Zǐgòng did not understand.
Confucius said,
"Earth,
if you dig it, you get sweet spring water;
if you plant on it, you get the five grains;
grasses and trees grow in it;
birds, beasts, fish, and turtles thrive in it;
when they are born, they stand on it;
when they die, they enter it;
it performs many services without speaking;
its benefits to the world are never-ending.
Therefore, it is said that one who can be subordinate
is like earth!"
Zǐgòng said,
"Though Cì is not clever,
I will put this saying into practice."
*Shuō Yuàn · Chén Shù*. Zǐgòng asked Confucius,
"Cì wishes to be subordinate to others,
and did not yet know the way to be subordinate to others."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"To be subordinate to others,
is like the earth!
Plant seeds in it, and the five grains will grow;
dig into it, and sweet springs will emerge;
grasses and trees are planted in it;
birds and beasts are nurtured in it;
the living stand upon it;
the dead enter into it;
it performs its many functions without speaking."
To be subordinate to others,
is like the earth!"
*Qúnshū Zhìyào*, *Shīzǐ · Míngtáng* Kǒngzǐ said:
"How great are the rivers and seas!
They are lowly."
The rivers receive the streams of the world,
therefore they are broad;
people treat the scholars of the world with respect,
therefore they are great."
*Qúnshū Zhìyào*, *Shīzǐ · Chǔdào* Zhòng Ní said:
"He who obtains it in himself obtains it from the people;
he who loses it in himself loses it from the people;
without going out of his door, he knows the world;
without descending from his hall, he governs the four directions.
This is because he understands the principle of looking inward to oneself."
*Shuō Yuàn · Jìngshèn* Kǒngzǐ saw fowlers,
and all they caught were young birds with yellow beaks.
Confucius said:
"Young birds are all obtained,
but large birds are never obtained.
Why is this?"
A fowler replied:
"Young birds that follow large birds cannot be obtained,
but large birds that follow young birds can be obtained."
Confucius turned and said to his disciples:
"A gentleman should be cautious of whom he follows;
if he does not find the right person, then he will suffer the calamity of a net."
Zēngzǐ said:
"I have heard the Master's three sayings,
but I have not been able to practice them.
The Master sees one good thing in a person and forgets their hundred faults;
this is the Master's ease in dealing with things.
The Master sees the good in others as if he himself possessed it;
this is the Master's lack of contention.
Upon hearing of good, he will certainly personally practice it
and then speak of it;
this is the Master's ability to exert himself.
The Master's ability to exert himself,
the Master's lack of contention,
the Master's ease in dealing with things -
I study the Master's three sayings but have not been able to practice them."
Confucius was about to travel
without a canopy.
A disciple said,
"Zǐxià has a canopy;
he can travel."
Confucius said,
"Shāng's character
is very deficient in regard to wealth.
I have heard that in dealing with people,
one should promote their strengths,
and avoid mentioning their weaknesses;
thus one can maintain a long-lasting relationship."
Zǐlù was about to travel and
took leave of Zhòngní, saying:
"May I ask how to make a new acquaintance become intimate?
How to ensure that few words are acted upon?
How to consistently be a good person without making mistakes?"
Zhòngní said:
"For a new acquaintance to become intimate,
be loyal;
for few words to be acted upon,
be trustworthy;
to consistently be a good person without making mistakes,
be respectful."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Who would not associate with someone who uses their wealth and status to humble themselves before others?
who would not associate with them?
Who would not feel close to someone who uses their wealth and status to respect and love others?
who would not be close to them?
Not contradicting the opinions of the many
can be considered understanding words;
being followed by the many
can be considered understanding the times."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"If one is wealthy and able to enrich others,
one cannot become poor even if one desires it.
If one is noble and able to ennoble others,
one cannot become base even if one desires it.
he cannot become lowly even if he desires to;
if one is successful and can make others successful,
he cannot become impoverished even if he desires to."
*Shuō Yuàn · Zá Yán*
Zhòngní said:
"If planted in a place not suited to it, it will not grow;
if spoken to a person not suited to it, they will not listen.
Attaining the right person
is like gathering sand and pouring water on it;
finding the wrong person
is like gathering the deaf and drumming for them."
*Shuō Yuàn · Zá Yán*
Kǒngzǐ said:
"A boat cannot travel without water,
but if water enters the boat, then it will sink."
Therefore, it is said that a *jūnzǐ* must be dignified,
and petty people must be restrained.
*Shuō Yuàn · Zá Yán*
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Relying on the virtuous, one will certainly not be distressed; relying on the wealthy, one will certainly not be impoverished.
Why does a horse with cracked and broken hooves continue to walk?
Because it has support from many feet."
*Shuō Yuàn · Zá Yán* Confucius said:
"If you do not know his son,
observe his friends.
If you do not know his ruler,
observe his envoys."
He also said:
"To dwell with good people
is like entering a room filled with orchids and *zhǐ* plants.
After a long time, you no longer smell their fragrance,
because you have become assimilated to it.
To dwell with bad people
is like entering a shop selling dried fish.
After a long time, you no longer smell their stench,
because you have also become assimilated to it."
*Zhōng Lùn · Guì Yàn* Confucius said:
"To live and gain worthy friends
is the next best thing to happiness."
On Judging People, Eight
*Yì Shǐ* 95, quoting *Shàngshū Dàzhuàn* Dōngguō Zǐsī asked Zǐgòng, saying:
"The Master's (Confucius') door
why is it so mixed?"
Zǐgòng said:
"Beside the straightening frame, there are many crooked timbers;
at the door of a good doctor, there are many sick people;
beside the whetstone, there are many dull blades."
The Master (Confucius) heard of this and said:
"I cultivate the Way to await the world.
Those who come do not cease.
Therefore, it is mixed."
*Shuō Yuàn · Zá Yán* (Garden of Stories · Miscellaneous Sayings): Dōngguō Zǐhuì asked Zǐgòng, saying:
"In the Master's school,
why is it so mixed?"
Zǐgòng said:
"Beside the straightening tool are many crooked pieces of wood;
at the door of a good doctor are many sick people;
beside the whetstone are many dull blades.
The Master cultivates the Way to await the whole world,
those who come do not stop,
therefore, it is mixed."
*Máo Shī · Xiàng Bó Zhuàn* (Mao Poems · Commentary on Lane Elder): In the past,
Yán Shūzǐ was alone in his room,
the widowed neighbor woman was also alone in her room,
a violent storm came at night and the room collapsed.
The woman hurried over,
Yán Shūzǐ let her in,
and had her hold a candle,
until dawn when the stalk was used up,
he made the house smaller to connect them.
He thought himself to be not cautious enough in avoiding suspicion.
If one were to be truly cautious,
one should be like the man of Lǔ.
A man of Lǔ was alone in his room,
the widowed neighbor woman was also alone in her room,
a violent storm came at night and the room collapsed.
The woman hurried over to seek shelter with him,
but the man closed the door and did not let her in.
The woman spoke to him from the window, saying:
"Why won't you accept me?"
The man said:
"I have heard it said that
a man should not live alone until he is sixty.
Now you are young,
and I am also young,
so I cannot accept you."
The woman said:
"Why can't you be like Liǔxià Huì?
An old woman led a girl who couldn't reach the door
and the people of the state did not call it disorder."
The man said:
"Liǔxià Huì was certainly capable,
but I am certainly not capable.
I will use my incapability to learn Liǔxià Huì's capability."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Those who want to learn from Liǔxià Huì have never been so close as this one."
*Han Poetry - Outer Commentary* 1 - When Jīng attacked Chén,
the west gate of Chén collapsed.
They used the surrendered people to repair it.
Kǒngzǐ passed by without bowing.
Zǐgòng held the reins and asked,
"According to ritual,
one bows when passing three people,
and makes a gesture when passing two.
Now there are many repairing the gate of Chén.
"Why don't you lean forward on the carriage bar, Master?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"To not know when a state is being destroyed is to be unwise;
to know but not to fight is to be disloyal;
to not die when a state is destroyed is to be cowardly.
Although those repairing the gate are many,
none of them are acting according to these principles, therefore I do not lean forward on the carriage bar."
*Shuō Yuàn · Lì Jié*: When Chǔ attacked Chén,
the west gate of Chén burned, so they made the surrendered people repair it.
Kǒngzǐ passed by it and did not lean forward on the carriage bar.
Zǐlù said:
"According to ritual, when passing three people, one should get out of the carriage;
when passing two people, one should lean forward on the carriage bar. Now, those repairing the gate of Chén are many people,
why do you not lean forward on the carriage bar, Master?"
Kǒngzǐ said: "I have heard that to not know when a state is being destroyed is unwise;
to know but not to fight is disloyal;
disloyal;
loyal but does not die for it;
unprincipled.
Now, those who seek to enter the gate of Chén Xiū
do not fail to do at least one of these things.
Therefore, Qiū would not do that for the sake of riding in carriages."
*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn* 2 Zǐlù and Wūmǎ Qī were gathering firewood below Yùnqīu.
A wealthy man from Chén named Chù Shīshì
had prepared a hundred carriages with oiled axles
and was holding a feast on Yùnqīu.
Zǐlù said to Wūmǎ Qī:
"If you were to forget what you know,
and suppress what you are capable of,
and gain this wealth,
never seeing the Master again for the rest of your life,
would you do it?"
Wūmǎ Qī sighed, looked up at the sky,
and threw his sickle on the ground, saying:
"I have heard the Master say:
'A brave man does not forget that he might lose his head,
and a person of determination and benevolence does not forget that he might end up in a ditch.'
Do you not know me?
Are you testing me?
Is this your true intention?"
Zǐlù felt ashamed,
so he carried the firewood back first.
Confucius said:
"Yóu, come here!
"Why is it that you went out together but returned first?"
Zǐlù said:
"Earlier, Yóu and Wūmǎ Qī had an appointment to gather firewood at the foot of Yùnqiū.
The Chén's wealthy man, named Chù Shīshì,
was holding a banquet with a hundred carriages adorned with fat,
on top of Yùnqiū.
Yóu said to Wūmǎ Qī,
'If you do not forget what you know,
and you do not advance your abilities,
and you obtain this wealth,
and for the rest of your life you never see the Master again,
would you do it?'
Wūmǎ Qī sighed, looked up to the sky, and lamented,
threw his sickle to the ground, and said,
'I have heard the Master say,
'A brave warrior does not forget losing his head,
A man of great aspiration and a person of benevolence do not forget being in a ditch.'
Do you not know me?
Are you testing me?
Perhaps this is my aspiration?'
Yóu felt ashamed in his heart,
so I carried the firewood back first."
Kǒngzǐ took up his qín and played it.
The *Shī* says:
"The bustard's feathers rustle,
gathered on the bushy oak.
The king's affairs are without end,
and I cannot cultivate millet and glutinous millet.
What can I rely on now that my parents are gone?
O vast blue heaven,
where can I turn!"
Is it that my way cannot be put into practice?
Those who caused you to wish this.
*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn* 2 Confucius said:
"There are five types of *shì*:
some are powerful and esteemed,
some are wealthy and prosperous,
some are naturally brave and fierce,
some are intelligent and wise,
and some are beautiful in appearance.
Those who are powerful and esteemed
do not use their power to love the people and practice righteousness,
but instead use it for violence and arrogance.
Those who are wealthy and prosperous
do not use their wealth to relieve the poor and rescue those in need,
but instead use it for extravagance and immoderate indulgence.
Those who are naturally brave and fierce
do not use their courage to defend their superiors and fight in battles,
but instead use it for aggression and private disputes.
Those who are intelligent and wise
do not use their intelligence to make proper calculations and plans,
but instead use it for cunning schemes and deceptive trickery.
Those who are beautiful in appearance
do not use their beauty to govern the court and oversee the people,
but instead use it to seduce and indulge their desires.
These five types
This is what is meant by a scholar losing his fine qualities."
*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn* 3: Shùn was born in Zhūféng,
moved to Fùxià,
and died in Míngtiáo.
He was a man of the Eastern Yi;
King Wén was born in Qízhōu,
and died in Bìyǐng.
He was a man of the Western Yi.
The distance between their locations
was more than a thousand *lǐ*,
and the separation between their generations
was more than a thousand years.
Yet, having achieved their ambitions, they practiced them in the Central Kingdom,
as if matching tallies.
Confucius said:
"Earlier sages and later sages,
their principles are the same."
*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn* 4: Confucius received a guest.
After the guest left,
Yán Yuān said:
"Was that guest benevolent?"
Confucius said:
"Resentment in his heart,
a troubled look on his face,
whether he is benevolent, I do not know.
He is a man of many words."
Yán Yuān, with a troubled expression, changed countenance and said:
"A fine jade of a foot in size,
Even with ten *rèn* of soil,
it cannot conceal its light;
a fine pearl of an inch,
even with a hundred *rèn* of water,
cannot conceal its brilliance.
Indeed, form and color, mind and heart,
are subtly and thinly manifested.
If there is warmth and goodness within,
then it will be evident in the eyebrows and eyelashes.
If flaws and imperfections are within,
then the eyebrows and eyelashes cannot conceal them."
The *Shī* says:
"The drums and bells are played in the palace,
their sound is heard outside."
*Yù Lǎn* 510 quotes *Gāo Shì Zhuàn* A guest came to visit Kǒngzǐ,
Yányuān asked,
"Who is this guest?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Xiāo xī fǎ xī,
I cannot fathom him.
A fine jade of one *chǐ* in diameter,
even ten *rèn* of soil cannot conceal its light;
a bright pearl of one *cùn* in diameter,
even a stone of a *hán zhàng* cannot diminish its radiance.
If he is warm and gentle,
his generous demeanor will be known."
*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn* 7 Kǒngzǐ was traveling on Jǐng Mountain,
Zǐlù, Zǐgòng, and Yányuān followed.
Confucius said:
"When a *jūnzǐ* ascends to a high place, he must compose a poem.
Those of you young ones who have wishes,
what are your wishes?
Qiū will elicit them from you."
Zǐlù said:
"Yóu wishes to brandish a long *jǐ*,
to sweep through the three armies,
with a tiger cub at my back,
and enemies before me,
like a *lí* leaping and a *jiāo* rising in vigor,
I would advance to save the disasters of two states."
Confucius said:
"A brave warrior!"
Zǐgòng said:
"When two states are engaged in conflict,
and brave warriors are arrayed in formation,
with dust clouds filling the sky,
Cì would not carry a single foot of weapon,
nor a single *dǒu* of grain,
but would resolve the difficulty of the two states.
Those who use Cì will survive,
those who do not use Cì will perish."
Confucius said:
"A skilled debater!"
Yānhuí did not state a wish.
Confucius said:
"Huí,
Why don't you wish for something?"
Yán Yuān 顏淵 said,
"These two have already wished,
so I dare not wish."
Confucius said,
"It's different;
their intentions each have their own matters.
Huí 回, if you wish,
I will enlighten you."
Yán Yuān 顏淵 said,
"I wish to obtain a small state and assist it.
The ruler governs with the Way,
the ministers transform through virtue,
ruler and ministers are of one mind,
and inside and outside correspond to each other.
The feudal lords of the various states
all follow righteousness and turn towards the wind of virtue,
the strong hasten to advance,
and the old are supported to arrive.
Teachings are practiced among the people,
and virtue is extended to the four barbarian tribes,
so that all lay down their weapons
and converge upon the four gates.
The world will all obtain lasting peace,
even the flying insects and wriggling creatures
will each enjoy their nature, advancing the worthy and employing the capable,
each taking responsibility for their tasks.
Thus, the ruler is at peace above,
The minister is in harmony with those below,
governing with folded hands and inaction,
acting according to the proper way,
being composed and adhering to propriety.
Those who speak of benevolence and righteousness are rewarded,
those who speak of warfare are put to death.
Then, what Hé Jìn would save,
what difficulty would Zì resolve?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"A sage is he!
When the great man appears,
the small man hides;
when the sage arises,
the worthy man submits.
If Huí were in power,
then what abilities would Yóu and Zì have to display!"
*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn*, Chapter 9. Kǒngzǐ was traveling on Mount Róng with Zǐgòng, Zǐlù, and Yányuān.
Kǒngzǐ sighed deeply and said:
"Each of you gentlemen, speak of your aspirations,
and I shall observe them.
Yóu, what about you?"
He replied:
"If I were given white-feathered arrows like the moon,
and red-feathered arrows like the sun,
and if I struck the bells and drums,
so that the sound was heard in Heaven above,
and thrust my spears into the ground below,
and ordered me to lead and attack,
only Yóu would be capable."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"A brave warrior indeed!
Zì, what about you?"
He replied:
"If I were given plain clothes and a white cap,
and be sent between two states,
without carrying an inch of weapon,
nor a peck or a斗 of grain,
causing the two states to be as close as brothers."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"What an eloquent debater!
Huí, what would you do?"
He replied:
"Salted fish should not be stored in the same basket as orchids and sweet herbs;
Jié and Zhòu should not rule at the same time as Yáo and Shùn.
The other two have already spoken,
what would Huí have to say?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Huí has a humble heart."
Yānyuān said:
"I wish to obtain an enlightened king and sage ruler to be his minister,
so that the city walls would not be repaired,
the moats would not be dug,
the yin and yang would be in harmony,
every household would be sufficient, and every person would be content,
and the weapons in the armory would be melted down into farming tools."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"What a great man!
Originally,
why would I attack you, a small person?
If you give to me,
what would I use you for, an eloquent person?
I wish to obtain your hat and appoint you as a local official."
Kǒngzǐ traveled north,
ascending Mount Nóng in the east.
Zǐlù, Zǐgòng, and Yānyuān followed him.
Kǒngzǐ sighed and said,
"Ascending high and looking down makes one's heart sad.
You three disciples,
each speak of your aspirations,
and I, Qiū, will listen."
Zǐlù said,
"I wish to obtain white feathers like the moon,
red feathers like the sun,
and the sound of bells and drums
reaching the heavens above.
With banners fluttering
and coiled upon the earth below,
I, Yóu, would raise an army and strike.
I would certainly seize land for a thousand *lǐ*,
only Yóu can do this.
And I would have those two as my followers."
Kǒngzǐ said,
"A brave warrior indeed!
"Are you all indignant!"
Zǐgòng said:
"Sì wishes for Qí and Chǔ to engage in a decisive battle on the plains of Mǎngyáng.
With their two camps facing each other,
banners and flags visible to each other,
dust clouds mingling,
and locked in combat.
Sì wishes to wear plain white robes and a white cap,
and deliver speeches amidst the flashing blades,
resolving the troubles of both nations.
Only Sì is capable of this.
I would have those two gentlemen follow me."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"What eloquent scholars!
How lofty!"
Yānhuí alone remained silent.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Huí, come here,
why do you alone have no wish?"
Yānhuí said:
"The matters of civil and military affairs
have already been spoken of by the two gentlemen.
How dare Huí participate!"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Even if your humble thoughts are not in agreement,
just speak them."
Yānhuí said:
"Huí has heard that salted fish and fragrant orchids
Stored in different boxes,
Yáo, Shùn, Jié, Zhòu,
ruled different states.
The words of you two
are different from Huí's words.
Huí wishes to obtain an enlightened king and sage ruler to assist,
so that city walls are not repaired,
moats are not crossed,
swords and spears are forged into agricultural tools,
and the world has no worry of war for a thousand years.
If it is like this,
then why should Yóu be so indignant and strike,
and what would Cì use his clever tongue for?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"How beautiful is this virtue!
How vast is it!"
Zǐlù raised his hand and asked,
"I wish to hear the Master's intention."
Kǒngzǐ said,
"What I desire
is the plan of the Yán family.
I wish to carry my robes and follow the son of the Yán family."
*Dà Dài Lǐ - Āi Gōng Wèn Wǔ Yì* (The Book of Great Dai - Duke Ai Asks About the Five Righteousnesses): Duke Āi of Lǔ asked Kǒngzǐ,
"I wish to evaluate the scholars of my state
and govern with them.
What kind of people should I choose?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"Living in today's world,
"To aspire to the ways of the ancients,
while living in the customs of the present,
and wearing the clothes of the ancients;
to abandon this and act wrongly,
would such a person not be rare indeed!"
Āi Gōng said:
"Then are all those today who wear the Zhāngfǔ cap, Jūjù shoes, and a Shēndài sash, and hold a Jìn Hù tablet,
all virtuous?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"No,
not necessarily.
Those today who wear the Dūānyī Yuáncháng crown and ride in a carriage,
may not be focused on abstaining from meat;
and those who wear mourning clothes, simple hemp shoes, and carry a staff, while drinking porridge,
may not be focused on food and drink.
Therefore, to be born in this present age,
aspire to the ways of the ancients,
live in the customs of the present,
and wear the clothes of the ancients;
to abandon this and act wrongly,
even if there are such people,
would they not be rare indeed!"
Āi Gōng said:
"Good.
What kind of person can be called mediocre?"
Kǒngzǐ replied:
"The so-called mediocre person
cannot speak good words, and their ambition is not fervent;
and whose will is not downcast;
who cannot select worthy and virtuous people to entrust themselves to,
and consider it their own concern;
whose actions do not know what to pursue,
whose efforts do not know where to settle,
who daily choose among things,
not knowing what is valuable;
who follow the current of things,
not knowing where to return;
who use the five openings for governance,
their hearts consequently corrupted.
Such a person
can be called a mediocre person."
Āi Gōng said,
"Good.
What must one be like to be called a shì?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"Those who are called shì,
though they may not fully master all arts and techniques,
must have something they follow;
though they may not be perfectly good and beautiful,
they must have a place where they abide.
Therefore, in knowledge, they do not strive for much,
but strive to examine what they know;
in action, they do not strive for much,
but strive to examine what they follow;
in speech, they do not strive for much,
but strive to examine what they say.
When knowledge has already been acquired,
when conduct has already been guided,
when words have already been made agreeable,
then one's nature, fate, and physical constitution cannot be easily altered.
Wealth and high status cannot increase them,
poverty and low status cannot diminish them.
If one is like this,
then he can be called a shì (士, scholar/gentleman)."
Āi Gōng said,
"Good.
What must one be like to be called a jūnzǐ (君子, noble person/gentleman)?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"The so-called jūnzǐ
personally practices loyalty and trustworthiness,
his heart is not for sale,
benevolence and righteousness reside within him,
yet he does not harm those without ambition.
He has heard of ambition widely and extensively,
but his countenance does not boast.
His thoughts and deliberations are clear and penetrating, but his words are not contentious.
The jūnzǐ seems approachable,
yet is unattainable.
If one is like this,
he can be called a jūnzǐ."
Āi Gōng said,
"Good.
May I venture to ask, what must one be like to be called a xiánrén (賢人, worthy person/sage)?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"The so-called worthy person,
their choices and rejections are in accord with the standards of the people,
their conduct is within the compass and line, yet does not harm the root (essence),
their words are sufficient to be a law to the world, yet do not harm themselves,
as a commoner, they wish for prosperity,
their likes and dislikes are in accord with the feelings of the people,
as a noble, they are without personal wealth.
Such a person
can be called worthy."
Āi Gōng said:
"Good.
May I ask, what can be called a sage?"
Kǒngzǐ answered:
"The so-called sage
is one whose knowledge is connected to the Great Dao,
responds to changes without exhaustion,
and is able to fathom the emotions and natures of all things.
The Great Dao
is that which transforms and congeals to form all things;
emotions and natures
are that by which right and wrong, acceptance and rejection are governed.
Therefore, their affairs are great,
matching Heaven and Earth,
participating with the sun and moon,
mingled with clouds and rainbows,
encompassing all things,
serene and pure,
none can follow their path,
It is like the administration of Heaven,
which no one can take over the duty of,
and the common people are indifferent and do not know its goodness.
If it is like this,
then it can be called a sage."
Āi Gōng said,
"Good."
Kǒngzǐ went out,
and Āi Gōng saw him off.
*Xúnzǐ·Āi Gōng* Duke Āi of Lǔ asked Kǒngzǐ,
"I want to evaluate the scholars of my state
and govern the state with them.
May I ask what would be best?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"Living in the present age,
aspiring to the ways of antiquity,
living according to contemporary customs,
wearing the clothes of antiquity,
and abandoning this to do wrong,
would that not be rare!"
Āi Gōng said,
"Then, are those who wear the pointed cap and hemp shoes, the sash, and hold a tablet,
are these virtuous?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"Not necessarily.
Those who wear proper robes and black skirts and possess talent yet ride in carriages,
their minds may not be on eating meat;
those who wear mourning clothes and straw sandals and lean on a staff while sipping gruel,
His ambition is not in wine and meat.
Living in this age,
aspiring to the ways of antiquity,
living amidst today's customs,
wearing the clothes of the ancients,
abandoning this to do something else,
even if there are such people,
wouldn't they be rare indeed!"
Āi Gōng said,
"Good!"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"People have five grades:
there are ordinary people (yōng rén),
there are shì,
there are jūnzi,
there are worthy people (xián rén),
there are great sages (dà shèng)."
Āi Gōng said,
"May I ask, what kind of person can be called an ordinary person?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"Those who are called ordinary people
cannot speak good words,
and their hearts do not understand beauty;
they do not know to choose worthy people and good shì to entrust their bodies to, so that they may worry on their behalf;
they diligently act but do not know what they should be doing;
they stop associating but do not know where they should settle;
they choose among things every day,
but do not know what is valuable;
They follow things like a flowing stream,
not knowing where to return;
they consider the five senses as correct,
and their hearts are thereby corrupted.
Such a person
can be called a commoner."
Āi Gōng said,
"Excellent!
May I ask, what kind of person can be called a shì (gentleman/scholar)?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"The so-called shì
may not be able to fully master the Dao and its techniques,
but they must have a guiding principle;
although they may not be able to embrace all goodness,
they must have a place to dwell.
Therefore, in knowledge, they do not strive for quantity,
but strive to examine what they know;
in speech, they do not strive for quantity,
but strive to examine what they say;
in action, they do not strive for quantity,
but strive to examine the path they follow.
Thus, once they have known what they know,
once they have said what they have said,
once they have followed the path they have chosen,
then it is as unchangeable as their own nature and skin.
Therefore, wealth and nobility cannot add to them,
and lowliness and poverty cannot diminish them.
Such a person
Then he can be called a shì (士, scholar/gentleman)."
Āi Gōng said,
"Excellent!
May I venture to ask, what must one be like to be called a jūnzǐ (君子, noble person)?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"The so-called jūnzǐ
speaks with loyalty and trustworthiness, and his heart does not dwell on self-merit;
rén (仁, benevolence) and yì (義, righteousness) are embodied in him, and his countenance is not boastful;
his thoughts are clear and penetrating, and his words are not contentious;
therefore, he remains approachable as if one could reach him at any moment.
This is a jūnzǐ."
Āi Gōng said,
"Excellent!
May I venture to ask, what must one be like to be called a xiánrén (賢人, worthy person)?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"The so-called xiánrén
acts within the bounds of propriety without harming the fundamentals;
his words are sufficient to be a model for the world without harming himself;
he possesses the wealth of the world yet bears no resentment towards wealth;
he bestows upon the world without being troubled by poverty.
Such a person
can be called a xiánrén."
Āi Gōng said,
"Excellent!
May I venture to ask, what must one be like to be called a dàshèng (大聖, great sage)?"
Kǒngzǐ replied,
"The so-called dàshèng
understands and is connected to the Great Dao;
To respond to changes without exhausting oneself
is to understand the feelings and natures of all things.
The Great Dao
is what transforms and completes all things.
Feelings and nature
are what govern right and wrong, taking and discarding.
Therefore, its operations are vastly discerning of Heaven and Earth,
clearly observing the sun and moon,
comprehensively gathering all things in wind and rain.
Subtle and sincere,
its operations cannot be followed.
Like the successor of Heaven,
its operations cannot be known.
The common people are so shallow that they do not know their neighbors.
If it is like this,
then it can be called a great sage."
Āi Gōng said:
"Good!"
*Dà Dài Lǐ - Wèi Jiāngjūn Wén Zǐ*: General Wèi, Wén Zǐ, asked Zǐ Gòng, saying:
"I have heard that the Master's teaching
begins with the *Book of Poetry*.
The way of the world is filial piety and fraternal duty,
explained with righteousness and observed in the body,
completed with literary virtue.
There are over seventy students who have received instruction.
Of them, who is considered virtuous?"
Zǐ Gòng replied,
declining with ignorance.
Wénzǐ said:
"My son studies with them,
how can you say you don't know them?"
Zǐgòng replied:
"The worthy do not act rashly,
but to truly know a worthy person is difficult.
Therefore, the gentleman says:
Nothing is more difficult than knowing a person.
This is why it is difficult."
Wénzǐ said:
"As for knowing the worthy,
everyone considers it difficult.
My son personally associates with them,
that is why I dare to ask."
Zǐgòng replied:
"The disciples of our master
can be roughly divided into three categories.
Cì is sometimes able to reach them,
and sometimes not,
and I cannot clearly discern them."
Wénzǐ said:
"Regarding those my son understands,
please tell me about their conduct."
Zǐgòng replied:
"Rising early and sleeping late,
reciting and upholding propriety,
never repeating a mistake,
and speaking truthfully,
This is the conduct of Yán Yuān.
Kǒngzǐ instructed him with the *Shī*,
The *Shī* says:
"Flatter this one person,
Respond to the prince with obedient virtue.
Ever speak of filial thoughts,
Filial thoughts are the standard."
Therefore, if a state happens to encounter a virtuous ruler,
He will inherit a renowned mandate through generations,
And not lose his name,
To be presented to the Son of Heaven to reiterate it.
Being poor as a guest,
Treating his ministers like mats,
Not transferring anger,
Not seeking resentment,
Not recording old offenses,
This is the conduct of Rǎn Yōng.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"There are gentlemen of service,
There are crowds to employ,
There are punishments to use,
And then he gets angry;
The anger of a common man
Only serves to destroy himself."
The *Shī* says, "Nothing does not have a beginning,
Few are able to have an end,"
To advise him.
Not fearing the powerful and violent,
He does not insult the lonely or widowed.
His words are about innate nature.
How abundant his wealth!
He shoulders military responsibilities.
This is the conduct of Zhòng Yóu.
The Master has not yet added refinement to it.
The *Shī* says, "Receiving the small and sharing the great,
Being sincerely attentive to the lower states,
What favor of Heaven
Has augmented and displayed their courage!"
He is truly strong and martial.
Refinement does not surpass his natural substance.
Respecting the elderly and caring for orphans,
Not forgetting guests and travelers,
Loving learning, examining things, but not being diligent,
This is the conduct of Rǎn Qiú.
Kǒngzǐ accordingly spoke to them, saying:
"Loving learning leads to wisdom,
Caring for orphans leads to kindness,
Respecting the elderly leads to being close to ritual propriety.
If one can be truly respectful, one can govern the world.
Praising him,
It is fitting that he should be a state elder."
His will is penetrating and he loves ritual propriety,
Serving as a master of ceremonies for two rulers.
How refined he is, possessing ritual propriety!
This is the conduct of Gōngxī Chì.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Three hundred rules of ritual and ceremony,
one can strive to master;
three thousand aspects of dignified bearing,
are then difficult."
Gōngxī Chì asked,
"What does this mean?"
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Appearance is used to usher in ritual,
ritual is used to usher in words,
this is what it means.
The host hears this and completes the process."
Kǒngzǐ, when talking to people, said:
"When dealing with matters of guests, then he is well-versed."
He said to his disciples:
"Those of you who wish to learn the etiquette of guests,
go to Chì."
Full yet not full,
substantial as if empty,
knowledgeable yet as if insufficient.
The elders value this,
not studying only appearances,
but pursuing virtue to its end,
enriching their words.
With regard to people,
they believe in everyone without exception.
The eminent elders always maintain a bright and clear appearance,
and thus enjoy long lives.
This is the conduct of Zēngshēn.
Confucius said:
'Filial piety
is the beginning of virtue; fraternal submission
is the order of virtue; trustworthiness
is the substance of virtue; loyalty
is the correctness of virtue.
Shēn,
he embodies these four virtues!'
This is how he praised him.
Not boasting of achievements,
not resenting high position,
not insulting the insulatable,
not neglecting the negletable,
not being arrogant to the helpless,
this is the conduct of Zhuānsūn.
Confucius said of him:
'That he does not boast
is still possible,
that he does not harm the common people
is benevolence.'
The Book of Odes says:
'The kind and gentle ruler
is the parent of the people.'
The Master considers his benevolence to be great.
Studying to be profound,
cultivating sharpness with determination,
treating departures and arrivals with reverence,
befriending superiors and associating with inferiors,
Like a silver hand severed,
this is the conduct of Bǔ Shāng.
Confucius said:
"The *Book of Poetry* says:
'Regulate yourself, regulate others,'
'there will be no harm from petty people.'
And Shāng,
it can be said that he is not dangerous."
Not pleased by honor,
not angered by disgrace,
if it is beneficial to the people,
being honest in his service to his superiors,
and assisting his subordinates,
this is the conduct of Tántái Mièmíng.
Confucius said:
"To be singularly honored and singularly wealthy
is a shame to the superior man,
and he is achieving it."
First completing his plans,
and then using them when the time comes,
therefore he does not forget,
this is the conduct of Yán Yǎn.
Confucius said:
"If you desire ability, then learn;
if you desire knowledge, then ask;
if you desire goodness, then inquire;
if you desire sufficiency, then prepare.
It can be said that Yǎn has attained these things."
Living alone, he thinks of benevolence;
speaking in public, he speaks of righteousness.
He heard it in the *Book of Poetry*.
Three times a day he recites the flaw in the white jade.
This is the conduct of Nángōng Tāo.
The Master believed in his benevolence
and considered him as someone outside his own clan.
Since meeting Kǒngzǐ,
upon entering the house, he never stepped over his shoes;
when walking back and forth, he would not step on people's shadows;
when the hibernating creatures emerged, he would not kill them;
when things were growing, he would not break them.
In observing the mourning for his parents,
his teeth were never seen [in laughter or eating].
This is the conduct of Gāo Chái.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Gāo Chái's observance of mourning for his parents
is indeed difficult to achieve;
not killing the hibernating creatures
accords with the way of Heaven;
not breaking things when they are growing
is forbearance.
Forbearance is benevolence.
Tāng was reverent and forbearing,
and thus he rose daily."
This is what Cì personally witnessed.
"If our master gives the order to inquire,
then Cì is not sufficient to know the worthy."
Wénzǐ said:
"I have heard it said that
when a state is governed by the Way, worthy people will rise up,
those of middling talent will be employed,
and the common people will turn to it.
If your words, my master, are truly substantial,
then you are fit to be a minister to a feudal lord,
but you have not yet encountered an enlightened ruler."
Zǐgòng, after speaking with Wèi General Wénzǐ,
went to Lǔ
and saw Kǒngzǐ, saying,
"The Wèi General asked Sì about the conduct of you gentlemen,
not just once but three times.
Sì declined, but could not avoid the request.
I answered with what I have seen myself.
I don't know if I hit the mark,
but I would like to tell you about it."
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Tell me."
Zǐgòng related the matter in its entirety.
After Kǒngzǐ heard it,
he laughed and said,
"Sì,
you think you know people well! Sì!"
Zǐgòng replied,
"How could Sì possibly know people?
These are things Sì has personally witnessed."
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Is he someone you are close to?
Let me tell you about
what your ears have never heard,
what your eyes have never seen,
what your thoughts have never reached,
and what your wisdom has never grasped?"
Zǐ Gòng said,
"If I may be so fortunate,
then I would like to hear it."
Kǒngzǐ said,
"Not being overcome by resentment,
not dwelling on past wrongs,
that is truly the conduct of Bó Yí and Shū Qí.
Duke Píng of Jìn asked Qí Xī,
'Yángshé, the Grand Master,
is a good Grand Master of the Jìn state.
How is his conduct?'
Qí Xī answered,
declining, saying,
'I do not know.'
The Duke said,
'I have heard that you grew up with him,
you should know him well.'
Qí Xī replied,
'In his youth, he was respectful and modest,
ashamed and not allowing his errors to linger overnight.
As a high official, he was entirely good,
and humble in his position.
When he served as the Gōngchē Wèi (Official in charge of Chariots), he was trustworthy,
and he liked to be straightforward in his achievements.
As for his being harmonious and accommodating,
he was gentle and kind, and fond of propriety;
he was widely learned and often expressed his aspirations."
The Duke said,
"Earlier, I asked you,
why did you say you did not know?"
Qí Xī replied,
"Each position changes,
and I do not know where it will end,
therefore I said I did not know."
He was Yángshé Dàfū in his conduct:
fearing Heaven and respecting people,
adhering to righteousness and acting with trustworthiness,
filial to his father and respectful to his elder brother,
fond of following good advice and quickly proceeding,
he was Zhào Wénzǐ in his conduct.
In serving his lord,
he did not dare to spare his life,
yet he also did not forget to plan for his own well-being;
he did not abandon his friends;
if the ruler deployed him, he advanced;
if not deployed, he withdrew and retreated,
he was Suí Wǔzǐ in his conduct.
In his being a wellspring for others,
he was widely knowledgeable and difficult to deceive;
he did not internalize words;
enough to finish one's life;
When the state is well-governed,
one's words are sufficient to preserve life;
When the state is not well-governed,
one's silence is sufficient to remain safe.
This is the conduct of Tóng Tí Bó Huá.
Outwardly lenient but inwardly upright,
he places himself within the bounds of propriety;
he is upright with himself but not demanding of others;
he preserves goodness,
and is not anxiously seeking wealth.
This is the conduct of Qú Bóyù.
Filial to parents and kind to the young,
he truly embodies virtue and possesses righteousness,
keeping possessions simple and avoiding resentment.
This is the conduct of Liǔxià Huì.
His words were:
"Though the ruler may not trust his minister,
the minister cannot but consider his ruler."
Therefore, the ruler chooses a minister to employ him,
and the minister chooses a ruler to serve him.
When the Way prevails, he complies with the ruler;
When the Way does not prevail, he defies commands.
This is the conduct of Yàn Píngzhòng.
His virtue is respectful and his conduct is trustworthy;
he speaks all day long,
but his words are not within the realm of blame,
but outside of it;
To be poor and yet joyful
is the conduct of Lǎo Lái Zi.
To easily practice virtue and await Heaven's Mandate,
to dwell in a humble position and not rely on superiors,
to observe the four directions,
to not forget one's parents,
if one but thinks of one's parents,
one cannot fully enjoy pleasure,
to take the inability to learn as a lifelong worry,
is the conduct of Jiè Shān Zǐ Tuī.”
*Qún Shū Zhì Yào*, *Shī Zi · Quàn Xué*. Confucius said:
"To find amusement in the confines of hidden principles,
to be straightforward with oneself but not with others,
to not be dejected when goodness is abandoned,
is the conduct of Qū Bó Yù.”
*Gǔ Liáng*, the fifth year of Duke Cheng’s reign. The collapse of Mount Liáng
dammed and stopped the river's flow for three days.
The ruler of Jìn summoned Bó Zūn and asked him about it.
Bó Zūn was coming
when he encountered sedan carriers.
The sedan carriers did not make way.
He ordered the charioteer to get down and whip them.
The sedan carrier said:
"The reason you whip me
must be that you are traveling a long distance!"
Bó Zūn got out of the carriage and asked him, saying:
"Have you heard something?"
He replied:
"Mount Liáng collapsed,
damming and stopping the river's flow for three days."
Bó Zūn said:
"The ruler summoned me for this reason.
What should be done about it?"
The sedan carrier said:
"Could Bózōng 伯尊 have no achievements?
He rejected goodness."
*Han Shi Waizhuan*, 8. When Mount Liáng 梁 collapsed,
the ruler of Jìn 晉 summoned the high official Bózōng 伯宗.
On the way, he encountered a carriage driver,
because of the driver's carriage attire.
Bózōng 伯宗 ordered his attendant to dismount,
intending to whip the driver.
The carriage driver said,
"The ruler hastens along the road,
is it not far?
To act without knowing the matter,
is that permissible?"
Bózōng 伯宗 was pleased
and asked where he lived. He replied,
"I am a person from Jiàng 絳."
Bózōng 伯宗 said,
"Have you also heard about it?" He said,
"Mount Liáng 梁 collapsed,
blocking the river,
causing it to not flow for three days,
and that is why you were summoned."
Bózōng 伯宗 said,
"What should be done?" He said,
"Heaven has a mountain,
Heaven caused it to collapse;
Heaven has a river,
Heaven blocked it.
"What will Bózōng do?"
Bózōng privately inquired about it, saying:
"Let your lord lead the assembled ministers in wearing white and mourning him;
then offer sacrifices to him,
and the river will flow again."
Bózōng asked his name,
but he did not tell him.
Bózōng arrived,
and the lord asked Bózōng,
who replied with his words.
Thereupon, the lord wore white, led the assembled ministers, and mourned him;
then offered sacrifices to him,
and the river flowed again.
The lord asked Bózōng how he knew this,
Bózōng did not say he received the instructions from the cart-puller,
falsely claiming to know it himself.
Kǒngzǐ heard of this and said:
"Bózōng will have no descendants!
Stealing other people's goodness."
*Lǔ Yǔ* (Discourses of Lu) II. Gōngfǔ Wénbó retired from court
and went to see his mother,
who was spinning.
Wénbó said:
"Even in the house of the Zhù family, the mistress is still spinning.
I fear offending Jìsūn's anger.
Could he think that I, Zhù, am unable to serve him?"
His mother sighed and said:
"Lǔ will perish!
Are you preparing your attendants as officials without informing me? Wait,
I will tell you.
In the past, when sage kings governed the people,
they chose barren lands to settle them,
exhausting and employing their people.
Therefore, they long reigned over the world.
When the people are weary, they ponder;
when they ponder, good intentions arise.
Ease leads to dissipation;
dissipation leads to forgetting goodness;
forgetting goodness leads to the arising of evil intentions.
The people of fertile lands are untalented,
due to dissipation.
The people of barren lands,
none do not incline towards righteousness,
due to their toil.
Therefore, the Son of Heaven would broadly gather at sunrise,
and with the Sāngōng (三公) and Jiǔqīng (九卿) would venerate the spirits of the land,
and at midday he examined the government,
handling state affairs with the various officials.
The Shīyǐn (師尹) would guide and the Mùxiàng (牧相) would proclaim and order the affairs of the people.
At the minor gathering at sunset,
with the Tàishǐ (太史) and Sīzǎi (司載), he investigated and reverently executed celestial punishments.
At sunset, he oversaw the nine Yù (禦),
ensuring they devoutly prepared the offerings for the Di (禘) and suburban sacrifices,
and only then did he rest, ensuring the feudal lords attended court and cultivated the Son of Heaven's ordained tasks.
During the day, he examined their national duties;
in the evening, he inspected their statutes and laws;
At night, supervise the various craftsmen
so that they are not dissolute or excessive,
and only then retire to rest.
The qing (卿) and dafu (大夫) in the morning examine their duties,
in the daytime discuss the various administrative affairs,
in the evening arrange their tasks,
at night manage their household affairs,
and only then do the shi (士) retire to rest.
In the morning, receive instruction;
in the daytime, practice thoroughly;
in the evening, review what has been learned;
at night, reflect on mistakes and have no regrets,
and only then retire to rest.
From the common people downwards,
move in the light
and rest in the darkness,
with no day spent in idleness.
The queen personally weaves black cords,
the wives of the dukes and marquises add to them with cords and streamers,
the wives of the qing (卿) make large belts,
the women of rank complete the sacrificial garments,
and the wives of the lie shi (列士) add to them with court robes.
From the common shi (士) downwards,
all are clothed by their wives.
At the local community sacrifice, tasks are assigned;
at the winter sacrifice, merits are presented;
men and women display their accomplishments,
and faults are punished;
This is the ancient system.
The noble man labors with his mind,
the small man labors with his strength;
this is the instruction of the former kings.
From those above to those below,
who would dare indulge their minds and abandon their strength?
Now I am bereaved,
and you are in a lower position;
attending to affairs morning and evening,
you are still afraid of forgetting the work of our ancestors,
how much more so if you are lazy?
How can you avoid disgrace?
I hope that morning and evening you will remind me, saying:
"You must not abandon the former men."
And now you say:
"Why not be at ease?"
Taking on the duties of a ruler with this attitude,
I fear the line of Mù Bó will be cut off."
Zhòng Ní heard this and said:
"Disciples, remember this:
The wife of the Jì family will not be licentious."
*Lǔ Yǔ* (Discourses of Lǔ), Part Two. Gōngfǔ Wénbó's mother
was the paternal cousin-aunt of Jì Kāngzǐ.
Kāngzǐ went to her,
[standing at the] gate and speaking with her,
never crossing the threshold.
When sacrificing to Dàozǐ,
Kāngzǐ participated.
He does not receive the sacrificial meat before the dishes are removed, nor does he feast;
the ancestral temple is not fully equipped, nor is the sacrifice fully examined;
if the examination of the sacrifice is not completely satisfying, then he withdraws.
Zhòngní 仲尼 heard of this
and considered it a distinction in the rites between men and women.
*Lǔ Yǔ*, part 2. Gōngfǔ Wénbó 公父文伯 died,
and his mother cautioned his concubines, saying:
"I have heard that
if he loved the inner quarters (women),
the women must die with him;
if he loved the outer affairs (men),
the gentlemen must die with him.
Now my son has died young,
and I would hate for him to be known for loving the inner quarters.
You, the concubines, who have the honor of jointly preceding in the sacrifices,
please show no emaciated faces,
shed no continuous tears,
do not clutch your breasts,
show no grieving expressions,
if you have mourning attire that is lower in status,
do not add attire that is higher in status,
follow the rites and be quiet;
this will honor my son."
Zhòngní 仲尼 heard of this and said:
"No one knows a woman better than a wife,
and no one knows a man better than a husband.
The wife of Gōngfǔ 公父,
She wishes to make clear her son's virtuous character."
*Lǔ Yǔ*, part 2. The mother of Gōngfǔ Wénbó 公父文伯 mourned Mù Bó 穆伯 in the morning and mourned Wénbó 文伯 in the evening.
Zhòngní 仲尼 heard of this and said:
"The wife of the Jì 季 family
can be said to know the rites.
She loves without being partial.
and there is order between superiors and inferiors."
*Yànzǐ Chūnqiū* (The Annals of Yanzi)·"Admonishing the Ruler": During the time of Duke Jǐng,
it snowed for three days without ceasing.
The Duke wore a white fox fur coat
and sat on the steps beside the hall.
Yànzǐ entered to see him
and stood there for a while.
The Duke said,
"How strange!
It has snowed for three days, yet the weather is not cold."
Yànzǐ replied,
"Is the weather not cold?"
The Duke laughed.
Yànzǐ said,
"I have heard that wise rulers of old knew the hunger of the people when they were full,
knew the cold of the people when they were warm,
and knew the toil of the people when they were at ease.
Now, you do not know this."
The Duke said,
"Good!
I have received your instruction."
He then ordered that fur coats and grain be distributed
with hunger and cold.
Order that those seen on the roads,
their native places not be asked;
those seen in the neighborhoods,
their families not be asked;
follow the state's accounting,
is wise indeed!
their names not be spoken.
Scholars already serving will be paid for extra months,
those who are ill will be supported for extra years.
Kǒngzǐ heard of this and said:
"Àn Zǐ is able to clarify what he desires,
Jǐng Gōng is able to put his good intentions into practice."
*Àn Zǐ Chūnqiū · Jiàn Xià*. Jǐng Gōng's favorite concubine, Yīng Zǐ, died.
The duke stayed by her side,
not eating for three days,
his skin sticking to the mat, unable to leave.
Those on his left and right tried to persuade him,
but the ruler would not listen.
Àn Zǐ entered
and reported, saying:
"A sorcerer and a doctor both say, 'We heard that Yīng Zǐ died of illness,
and we wish to request to treat her.'"
The duke was delighted
and quickly rose, saying:
"Can the illness still be remedied?"
Àn Zǐ said:
"These are the methods of sorcerers,
who claim to be good doctors.
Please allow them to try.
Your Lordship should please withdraw,
cleanse yourself with bathing and eating,
and distance yourself from the palace of the sick one;
they will also have spiritual matters to attend to."
The duke said:
"Agreed."
He withdrew and bathed.
Yàn Zǐ ordered the coffin bearers to enter and prepare the body for burial.
Once the body was prepared,
he further said:
"The doctor could not cure the illness.
The body has already been prepared,
but I dare not fail to report this."
The Duke, displeased, changed his expression and said:
"The master relied on the doctor to preserve my life,
but did not allow me to see him.
Now, about to bury him, you did not report it.
My position as ruler
is merely in name only."
Yàn Zǐ said:
"Does Your Lordship not know that the dead cannot be brought back to life?
I have heard that,
when the ruler is upright and the ministers follow, it is called obedience;
when the ruler is perverse and the ministers follow, it is called defiance.
Now, Your Lordship does not follow the path of obedience but acts perversely.
Those who follow evil are close,
while those who guide against harm are distant.
When flattery and deceit flourish,
wise and virtuous men are discarded.
Therefore, sycophants abound in the court,
and wicked deeds permeate the nation.
In the past, my former lord Duke Huán (Huán Gōng) achieved hegemony by employing Guǎn Zhòng,
but was ruined by indulging Shù Diāo.
Now, Your Lordship is deficient in treating worthy men with respect, yet excessive in grieving for a concubine.
Furthermore, the ancient sage kings indulged private affections without harming conduct,
mourned the dead without losing love,
and saw the dead off without abandoning grief.
Harmful conduct drowns oneself,
loss of love injures life,
and loss of grief harms nature.
Therefore, the sage kings regulated these things.
Once the burial is complete,
do not prolong the affairs of the living.
The coffin, outer coffin, clothing, and shroud
should not harm the living.
Weeping and lamenting in mourning
should not harm the way of life.
Now, preserving a decaying corpse affects the living,
excessive love injures conduct,
and prolonged grief harms nature.
Your Lordship is mistaken.
Therefore, the guests of other lords are ashamed to enter our state,
and the ministers of our court are ashamed to maintain their positions.
Exalting Your Lordship’s behavior
cannot guide the people,
Following your desires
is not the way to maintain a state.
Moreover, Yīng has heard that
leaving a corpse to rot unburied is called exposing the corpse to shame (lù shī),
leaving it to stink uncollected is called displaying the decayed flesh (chén zì).
This goes against the nature of an enlightened ruler,
invites the slander of the common people,
and favors concubines amidst rotting corpses.
This is why it is unacceptable."
The Duke said,
"I was unaware.
I ask to act according to your guidance, Master."
Yàn Zǐ again said,
"The state's officials, grand officers, feudal lords, and neighboring guests
are all outside.
May Your Lordship mourn appropriately and restrain yourself."
Zhòng Ní heard of this and said,
"The brightness of the stars
is not as good as the faint light of the moon.
The accomplishment of small matters
is not as good as the abandonment of great matters.
The disapproval of a gentleman
is better than the approval of a petty person.
This must be what Yàn Zǐ meant!"
"Yàn Zǐ Chūn Qiū, Miscellaneous I" Duke Píng of Jìn wanted to attack Qí,
and sent Fàn Zhāo to observe them.
Duke Jǐng feasted him.
The drinking became intense,
Fàn Zhāo said,
"Please have your wine vessel discarded."
The Duke said,
"I pour from my own vessel,
and offer it to my guests."
Fàn Zhāo had already drunk.
Yàn Zǐ said,
"Remove the vessel,
and change it."
The vessels were prepared.
Fàn Zhāo feigned drunkenness,
displeased and rose to dance,
saying to the Grand Musician,
"Can you tune the music of Chéngzhōu for me?
I will dance it for you."
The Grand Musician said,
"Your humble servant is not familiar with it."
Fàn Zhāo hurried out.
Duke Jǐng said to Yàn Zǐ,
"Jìn is a great state,
sending a messenger to observe our government.
Now you have angered the envoy of a great state,
what will we do?"
Yàn Zǐ said,
"Fàn Zhāo's behavior,
is not from ignorance or lack of etiquette,
but he intends to test our ruler and ministers,
therefore he was rebuffed."
Duke Jǐng of Qí said to the Grand Music Master:
"Why don't you prepare the music of the Zhōu capital for our guest?"
The Grand Music Master replied:
"The music of the Zhōu capital
is the music of the Son of Heaven.
If it is prepared,
the ruler must dance to it.
Now Fàn Zhāo is a subject,
and he wishes to dance to the music of the Son of Heaven.
Therefore, I would not prepare it."
Fàn Zhāo returned and reported to Duke Píng of Jìn, saying:
"Qí is not yet to be attacked.
I wanted to test their ruler, and Yàn Zǐ recognized it.
I wanted to violate their propriety, and the Grand Music Master knew it."
Zhòng Ní heard this and said:
"To know events a thousand *lǐ* away without leaving the space between the honored mats and the sacrificial stands,
that is what they mean by Yàn Zǐ.
He can be called one who blunts the enemy's attack!
And the Grand Music Master participates in it."
*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn*, Chapter 8: Duke Píng of Jìn sent Fàn Zhāo to observe the government of the Qí state.
Duke Jǐng provided him with a banquet.
Yàn Zǐ was present.
Fàn Zhāo hurried forward and said:
"I wish the ruler would offer a cup of the wine he drinks from as a toast to me."
Duke Jǐng looked to his attendants and said:
"Pour from my cup and present it to the guest."
Fàn Zhāo drank.
Yàn Zǐ replied:
"Remove the wine vessels."
Fàn Zhāo did not approve.
He rose to dance,
and turned to the grand musician, saying:
"Please play the music of Chéngzhōu for me,
for I wish to dance."
The grand musician replied:
"This blind servant is not familiar with it."
Fàn Zhāo rose,
and went out the door.
Duke Jǐng said to Yànzi:
"The state of Jìn
is a great state in the world.
They sent Fàn Zhāo to observe the government of the state of Qí.
Now you have angered the envoy of a great state,
what will be the consequence?"
Yànzi said:
"Fàn Zhāo's character
is not so ignorant as to not know propriety,
he intends to test our lord.
Therefore, I did not comply."
Thereupon Duke Jǐng summoned the grand musician and asked him, saying:
"Fàn Zhāo had you play the music of Chéngzhōu,
why did you not perform?"
He answered as Yànzi had said.
Thereupon Fàn Zhāo returned and reported to Duke Píng, saying:
"Qí cannot be annexed yet.
I tested their lord,
Yàn Zǐ knew it;
I trespassed on their music,
the Grand Music Master knew it."
Kǒngzǐ heard this and said,
"Excellent!
Yàn Zǐ, without leaving the space between the sacrificial vessels,
repelled enemies a thousand *lǐ* away."
*Xīn Xù · Zá Shì* 1. Duke Píng of Jìn wanted to attack Qí,
and sent Fàn Zhāo to observe them.
Duke Jǐng bestowed gifts upon him.
After the wine had flowed freely,
Fàn Zhāo said,
"I wish to request a drink from your Lordship's goblet."
The Duke said,
"Pour from my goblet
and offer it to the guest."
Fàn Zhāo finished drinking.
Yàn Zǐ said,
"Remove the goblet
and replace it."
The goblet and cup were prepared.
Fàn Zhāo feigned drunkenness,
displeased, and began to dance,
saying to the Grand Music Master,
"Can you perform the music of the Zhōu capital for me?
I will dance it for you."
The Grand Music Master said,
"Your humble servant is not familiar with it."
Fàn Zhāo hurried out.
Jǐng Gōng said to Yàn Zǐ,
"Jìn is a great state,
and they have sent a messenger to observe our government.
Now you have angered the messenger from the great state,
what will we do?"
Yàn Zǐ said,
"As for Fàn Zhāo's character,
it is not that he is ignorant and does not know propriety,
but he intended to test our ruler and ministers,
therefore I cut him off."
Jǐng Gōng said to the Grand Musician,
"Why did you not tune the music of Chéng Zhōu for the guest?"
The Grand Musician replied,
"The music of Chéng Zhōu,
is the music of the Son of Heaven,
if I were to tune it,
then the ruler must dance to it.
Now Fàn Zhāo is a subject,
but wants to dance to the music of the Son of Heaven,
therefore I did not do it."
Fàn Zhāo returned and reported to Píng Gōng,
"Qí cannot be attacked.
I wanted to test their ruler and Yàn Zǐ recognized it,
I wanted to violate their propriety and the Grand Musician knew it."
Zhòng Ní heard of this and said,
"To know what is happening a thousand miles away without leaving the table,
that is what Yàn Zǐ is like!
It can be said he settled disputes;
and the Grand Tutor was involved in this."
*Yàn Zǐ Chūnqiū · Zá Shàng* Yàn Zǐ was observing the mourning for Yàn Huánzǐ,
wearing coarse hemp mourning clothes, with a hemmed edge,
a hemp mourning band and belt, and a staff,
hemp sandals,
eating gruel,
living in a lean-to beside the grave,
sleeping on straw matting,
and using grass as a pillow.
His steward said,
"This is not the proper mourning ritual for a *dàfū* who has lost his father."
Yàn Zǐ said,
"Only a *qīng* is considered a *dàfū*."
Zēng Zǐ told Kǒngzǐ about this,
and Kǒngzǐ said,
"Yàn Zǐ can be said to be good at avoiding harm.
He does not use his own right to refute the wrong of others,
but uses humble words to avoid blame;
this is righteous indeed!"
*Xúnzǐ · Dàlüè* The Master said that Zǐjiā Jū, though a continuing *dàfū*,
was not as good as Yàn Zǐ.
Yàn Zǐ
was a minister of practical use,
but not as good as Zǐchǎn.
Zǐchǎn
was a benevolent man,
but not as good as Guǎn Zhòng.
Guǎn Zhòng's character was such that
he emphasized achievement over righteousness,
he emphasized knowledge over benevolence.
He was a commoner.
He could not be made emperor or high official.
*Xúnzǐ · Zidào* Zǐlù asked Confucius,
"Is it proper ritual
for a Lǔ high official to use plain white silk on his bed?"
The Master said,
"I do not know."
Zǐlù went out
and said to Zǐgòng,
"I thought the Master knew everything,
but the Master doesn't know something."
Zǐgòng said,
"What did you ask?"
Zǐlù said,
"Yóu asked, 'Is it proper ritual
for a Lǔ high official to use plain white silk on his bed?'
The Master said, 'I do not know.'"
Zǐgòng said,
"I will ask for you."
Zǐgòng asked,
"Is using plain white silk on a bed
proper ritual?"
Confucius said,
"It is not proper ritual."
Zǐgòng went out
He said to Zǐlù:
"Do you think that Fūzǐ (Confucius) has something he doesn't know?
Fūzǐ simply knows everything,
your question is inappropriate. According to ritual,
living in this city,
you should not criticize its senior officials."
*Xúnzǐ·Āigōng* Duke Āi of Lǔ asked Confucius, saying:
"May I ask about selecting people?"
Confucius replied, saying:
"Do not select the forceful,
do not select the dissolute,
do not select the verbose. Forceful means
greedy; dissolute means
disorderly;
verbose means
boastful.
Therefore, after a bow is tuned, then seek its strength;
after a horse is trained, then seek its goodness;
after a man is trustworthy and sincere, then seek his wisdom and ability.
If a man is not trustworthy and sincere but has much wisdom and ability,
it is like a jackal or wolf,
you cannot be close to him.
The saying goes:
'Duke Huán employed his enemies,
Duke Wén employed his thieves.'
Therefore, an enlightened ruler relies on plans and does not trust anger;
a foolish ruler trusts anger and does not rely on plans.
He who uses plans to overcome anger is strong;
"One who lets anger overcome strategy will perish."
*Hán Shī Wài Zhuàn* (韓詩外傳), Scroll 4. Āi Gōng (哀公) asks about selecting people.
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"Do not select the strong;
do not select the flattering;
do not select the slanderous. Strength
is arrogance; flattery
is sycophancy; slander
is falsehood.
Therefore, a bow is adjusted
and then strength is sought in it;
a horse is tamed
and then its quality is sought;
a man is trustworthy and sincere,
and then knowledge is sought in him.
If a man is untrustworthy
and also very knowledgeable,
he is like a jackal or wolf,
and it is difficult to get close to him.
The *Zhōu Shū* (周書) says:
