*Shuō Yuàn · Zūn Xián* (說苑·尊賢). Āi Gōng (哀公) asked Kǒngzǐ (孔子) saying:
"What kind of person is suitable to select?"
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) replied, saying:
"Do not select the tight-lipped,
do not select the clever,
do not select the sharp-tongued."
Āi Gōng said:
"What does this mean?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Those who are clever with their hands are greatly skilled and efficient,
but they use their skills completely without restraint.
Those who are quick-witted invariably desire to dominate others,
and cannot be taken as models.
Those who are sharp-tongued are often prone to exaggeration and lack credibility;
in the end, one fears their words will not be fulfilled.
Only when bows and arrows are harmonious and well-tuned
do you then seek to find their true center.
Only when horses are honest and willing
do you then seek out their good qualities.
Only when people are loyal, trustworthy, and dignified
do you then seek out their wisdom and ability.
If a person is not loyal, trustworthy, or dignified, yet possesses much wisdom and ability,
such a person
is comparable to a jackal or wolf,
and cannot be approached closely.
Therefore, first prioritize those who are sincere in benevolence and trustworthiness,
and then befriend them.
Only then, if they possess wisdom and ability,
should you entrust them with responsibilities.
Hence it is said, 'Befriend the benevolent and employ the capable.'
The art of selecting people
lies in observing their words and examining their actions.
Words are the means by which one expresses what is in one's heart and reveals one's feelings.
Those who are capable of action
Certainly be able to discern it by their words,
therefore, first observe their words and then assess their actions.
Even if there are treacherous and deceitful people,
there is no way for them to escape being exposed."
Āi Gōng said,
"Excellent."
《Lièzǐ·Tiān Ruì》 Confucius was traveling on Mount Tài,
and saw Róng Qǐqī walking in the fields of Chéng.
He was wearing a deerskin coat and a rope belt,
playing the qín and singing.
Confucius asked,
"Sir, what is the reason for your happiness?"
What is it?"
He replied,
"I have many reasons for happiness:
Heaven created all things,
and humans are the most noble,
and I have been able to become a human,
this is one happiness;
there is a distinction between male and female,
men are honored and women are lowly,
therefore being a man is considered noble,
and I have already become a man,
this is the second happiness;
in life, some do not see the sun and moon, and do not escape being swaddled,
and I have already reached the age of ninety,
this is the third happiness.
Poverty is the norm for scholars,
Death is the end of a person's life.
To abide in the constant and attain the end,
what is there to worry about?"
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Excellent!
He is one who can comfort himself."

Fierce winds and heavy rains,

those who appear compliant but are ambitious,

*Imperial Readings of the Taiping Era*, 915, quotes *Zhuāngzǐ*. Lǎozǐ met Kǒngzǐ,

*Lǚshì Chūnqiū·Shì Jūnlǎn·Zhī Fēn* 呂氏春秋·恃君覽·知分 Jīng 荊 had a man named Cì Fēi 次非,

*Huáinánzǐ · Dào Yīng Xùn* There was a man of Jīng named Cì Fēi,

"I have never seen it."

Confucius heard of this and said,

*Xīn Xù · Zá Shì* 4. The people of Zhèng gathered in the village school,
to discuss the merits and demerits of the government.
Rán Míng said to Zǐchǎn:
"Why not destroy the village school?"

"Why would I?
People come here morning and evening,
to discuss the merits and demerits of the government.
What they deem good,
I will implement;
what they dislike,

I have heard that one should diminish resentment through loyalty and trustworthiness in governing,
I have not heard of using intimidation to prevent resentment.

If a large breach occurs,
the damage to people will inevitably be great,
and I will be unable to save them.

"Indeed,
now I know that your sincerity, Master, is trustworthy and that you can be served.
I am truly untalented.

the state of Zhèng will truly rely on it,

"Judging from this,
people say that Zǐchǎn is not benevolent,

*Shuō Yuàn·Lì Jié* Zēng Zǐ tilled the land wearing worn-out clothes.

Dōnglǘ Zǐ once wealthy and noble, later became a beggar.
Someone asked him:
"Why are you like this, sir?" He said:
"I know it myself.
I once served as prime minister for six or seven years,
and never recommended a single person;
I was once wealthy with thirty million twice,
and never enriched a single person.
I don't know but this is the fault of my seven times of advancement."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Things are difficult,
whether small or large, few or many,

when a person obtains them, it is because he relies on external assistance."
Zǐlù asked Kǒngzǐ, saying:
"What kind of person was Guǎn Zhòng?"

"A great man."

Guǎn Zǐ tried to persuade Duke Xiāng,

He wanted to establish Gōngzǐ Jiū but couldn't;
this is a lack of ability.
His family suffered devastation in Qí, yet he showed no sign of worry;
this is a lack of compassion.
He was shackled and lived in a caged cart without a shameful expression;
this is a lack of shame.
He served the ruler who shot at him;
this is a lack of integrity.
Zhào Hū died for their cause,

"Guǎn Zhòng tried to persuade Duke Xiāng,

Guǎn Zǐ was not lacking in eloquence,

he was not lacking in ability,
but he did not have the opportune time.
His family suffered devastation in Qí, yet he showed no sign of worry;
he was not lacking in compassion,
but he understood fate.
He was shackled and lived in a caged cart without a shameful expression;
he was not lacking in shame,
but he was taking it upon himself.
He served the ruler who shot at him;
he was not lacking in integrity,
but he understood expediency.
Zhào Hū dies for his lord,
Guǎn Zǐ does not,
not because he is without benevolence.
Zhào Hū
is the stuff of which a minister is made;
if he did not die, he would become a prisoner of the enemy army;
if he dies, his name will be known throughout the world.
Why then should he not die?
Guǎn Zǐ,
on the other hand, is the assistant of the Son of Heaven, the prime minister of the feudal lords;
if he dies, he will merely become a starved corpse in a ditch;
if he does not die, his achievements can be used again for the benefit of the world.
Why then should he die? Yóu,
you do not understand this." 《Shuō Yuàn · Quánmóu》 Confucius asked Qīdiāo Mǎrén,

it is slight yet obvious.
Therefore, wisdom cannot reach it,
discernment cannot see it,
how can one avoid frequent divination?"
*Shuō Yuàn · Quánmóu* Zhōngháng Wénzǐ, fleeing into exile, arrived at the border.
His follower said:
"This local official,
a ruler of men,
why not rest here,
and wait for the following carriages?"
Wénzǐ said:
"Another day I liked music,
and this man gifted me a zither;
I liked ornaments,
He also sent me jade.
This shows he is not one who criticizes my faults,
but one who seeks to ingratiate himself with me.
I fear that he is using me to seek favor."
Therefore, he did not enter.
The carriage behind entered the gate.
Wénzǐ asked where the steward was,
seized him, and killed him.
Zhòngní heard of this and said,
"Zhōngxíng Wénzǐ abandoned the Way and lost righteousness, thus losing his state.
Afterwards, he obtained it,
yet managed to save his own life.
The Way cannot be abandoned;
it is like this."
*Shuō Yuàn · Zá Yán* Confucius said,
"Huí,
you possess four qualities of the way of a gentleman:
strong in conducting oneself,
weak in accepting admonishment,
fearful in awaiting emolument,
and cautious in maintaining one's integrity."
*Shuō Yuàn · Zá Yán* Zhòngní said,
"Shǐ Bīn has three qualities of the way of a gentleman:
he reveres his superiors without serving them,
he reveres spirits without sacrificing to them,
and he can yield to others despite being upright."
*Shuō Yuàn · Zá Yán* Confucius said,
"After my death,
Shāng is daily increasing,
Cì is daily diminishing.
Shāng likes to associate with those who are better than himself,
Cì likes to talk about those who are not as good as himself."
Prince Jìn, the heir of King Líng of Zhōu,
possessed accomplished virtue from a young age,
was intelligent and broadly knowledgeable,
and was gentle, respectful, earnest, and quick.
The Gǔ and Luò rivers fought,
threatening to destroy the royal palace,
and it was desired to dam them up.
Prince Jìn advised against it,
believing it would not be in accordance with the will of Heaven,
and that it would be better to rectify the government.
Duke Píng of Jìn sent Shū Yù as an envoy to Zhōu,
who met the Prince,
and spoke with him.
After five inquiries, he was stumped three times,
and retreated hesitantly.
Returning, he told Duke Píng:
"Prince Jìn is only fifteen years old,
yet I, Yù, could not converse with him.
Your Lordship should serve him."
Duke Píng sent Shī Kuàng to meet Prince Jìn.
Prince Jìn spoke with him,
and Shī Kuàng was impressed by his virtue,
forming a deep connection with him.
Thereupon, he asked Shī Kuàng:
"I have heard that Great Master, you can know the length of a person's life."
Shī Kuàng replied:
"A woman's complexion that is red and white,
a woman's voice that is clear and breathy,
a fire's color that isn't constant, do not last long."
Jìn said:
"Indeed.
Three years from now, I will ascend as a guest to the Emperor on High.
You must be careful not to speak of this,
or disaster will befall you."
Three years later, the heir apparent died.
Confucius heard of this and said,
"Alas!
He killed my lord."
*Yì Shǐ* 95, quoted in *Liú Qīng Rì Zhá*. Gōngyě Cháng was poor and lived in seclusion,
without means to provide for food.
A sparrow flew and chirped near his house,
calling to him,
"Gōngyě Cháng!
Gōngyě Cháng!
In the southern mountains, there is a tiger carrying a sheep,
you eat the meat,
I'll eat the intestines,
you should quickly go get it and do not hesitate!"
Zǐ Cháng acted according to what it said
and went to retrieve and eat it.
When the person who lost the sheep tracked it,
he found its horns,
Consequently, he was accused of theft.
They brought the case to the lord of Lǔ,
but the lord of Lǔ did not believe bird language
and had him arrested and imprisoned.
Kǒngzǐ had long known of this,
and pleaded his case to the lord of Lǔ,
but he would not understand.
Thereupon, he sighed and said,
"Although he is in bonds and chains,
it is not for his crime."
Before long,
while Zǐcháng was in the prison,
a sparrow again flew and chirped above him,
calling out:
"Gōngyě Cháng!
Gōngyě Cháng!
The army of Qí is invading our territory,
on the Yí River,
beside Mount Yì,
you must quickly defend against them, do not hesitate."
Zǐcháng had the prison warden inform the lord of Lǔ,
but the lord of Lǔ still did not believe it.
He tentatively followed his words,
and went to investigate,
and indeed the Qí army was about to arrive.
He urgently sent out troops to meet the enemy
and subsequently won a great victory.
Consequently, he released Gōngyě Cháng and richly rewarded him,
wanting to grant him the rank of senior official,
but he declined.
For he was ashamed to receive a reward due to his ability to understand the language of birds.
Later generations therefore abandoned this study.
On Government Nine
*Shàngshū Dàzhuàn*. The Master said:
"Those who listened to the people in ancient times
observed the poor and destitute,
pitied the orphaned and lonely,
showed compassion to widows,
pardoned the old and young,
provided for the unworthy who had no one to turn to,
certainly forgave those with transgressions,
did not increase minor offenses,
did not accumulate major offenses,
did not subject the old and weak to punishment,
did not fine those who had transgressed.
Therefore, punishing the old is called perverse,
punishing the weak is called inhumane,
not pardoning those with transgressions is called villainous,
and leading others into transgression with petty things is called obstructive.
Therefore, rather than killing an innocent person,
it is better to let a guilty one go free;
rather than adding to the punishment of someone guilty,
it is better to err on the side of pardoning their transgression."
When Confucius went to Wèi,
people said:
"Gōngfǔ is not capable of hearing lawsuits."
The Master said:
"It's not that Gōngfǔ 公甫 was incapable of hearing cases.
When Gōngfǔ 公甫 heard cases,
the guilty were fearful,
and the innocent felt ashamed.
The people were close to propriety."
*Shangshu Da Zhuan*
"Even if you grasp the essentials of hearing a lawsuit,
you must still have sorrow and compassion.
The dead cannot be brought back to life,
and what is severed cannot be rejoined.
The *Book* says,
'Sorrow and compassion in judging cases.'"
*Shangshu Da Zhuan*
"In the customs of Wú 吳 and Yuè 越,

Their punishments are severe and yet effective,

'The Xià Hòu 夏后 did not kill or inflict corporal punishment;

*Hòu Hàn·Wǔ Xíng Zhì* Commentary quoting *Shàngshū Dàzhuàn*, Zhèng’s Commentary: Confucius, in his explanation of the *Chūnqiū*, said:
"If the governance does not originate from the king,
it cannot be considered true governance.
Thus, the title of 'king' signifies that governance emanates from him."
*Hán Shī Wàizhuàn* 2: A high wall, thick at the top and tapering down,
may not necessarily collapse.
But when rain arises,
and flowing floodwaters arrive,
then its collapse will surely come first.
Plants and trees with shallow roots
may not necessarily be uprooted.
But when a whirlwind arises,
and a torrential rain falls,
then their uprooting will surely come first.
If a gentleman resides in a state,
but does not cultivate benevolence and righteousness,
respect worthy ministers,
and govern all things with reason,
it may not necessarily perish.
But once an extraordinary change occurs,
and the feudal lords engage in mutual conflict,
and people rush about in vehicles,
and disaster presses near,
only then do they begin to worry and be anxious,
with dry throats and parched lips,
looking up to the sky and sighing,
hoping to find some means of securing peace.
Is it not too late?
Confucius said:
"Not being cautious beforehand, and regretting it afterwards.
Alas!
Though one repents, it will be too late."
"Garden of Stories · Establishing the Foundation" A high wall under the eaves,
may not necessarily collapse;
but when a flood comes in torrents,
it will surely be the first to be destroyed.
A tree with shallow roots and a shallow foundation,
may not necessarily be uprooted;
but when a whirlwind arises,
and a heavy rain comes,
it will surely be the first to be uprooted.
A gentleman who lives in a country,
and does not value benevolence and righteousness,
and does not respect virtuous ministers,
may not necessarily perish.
However, once an extraordinary change occurs,
with chariots racing and people fleeing,
and disaster arriving when pointed at,
then they begin to have a dry throat and parched lips,
looking up to the sky and sighing,
hoping that Heaven will save them,
is that not difficult?
Confucius said:
"Not being careful beforehand and regretting it afterward,
though one repents, it will be too late."

The "Han Shi Waizhuan", chapter three, says:
"In Sòng, there was a great flood.
The people of Lǔ sent condolences, saying:
'Heaven sent excessive rain,
harming the millet offerings,
extending to your lord's territory,
causing worry to those in power;
your servant sends respectful condolences.'
The people of Sòng replied, saying:
'I, the lonely one, am not benevolent,
I did not properly observe fasts and abstinence,
I employed the people at the wrong times,
so Heaven inflicted this disaster,
and also caused worry to your lord.
I am ashamed to receive your command.'
Kǒngzǐ heard this and said:
'The state of Sòng is perhaps nearing good fortune!'
His disciple said:
'What do you mean?'
Kǒngzǐ said:
'In the past, Jié and Zhòu did not acknowledge their faults,
Their ruin is sudden.
Cheng, Tang, and King Wen knew how to acknowledge their mistakes,
their rise was vigorous.
To err and correct it,
that is not to err."
The people of Song heard this,
and thus rose early and slept late,
offered condolences to the dead and inquired after the sick,
and exerted their strength within the realm.
After three years,
the year was bountiful and the government peaceful."
*Han Shi Waizhuan*, Six. Zǐ Lù governed Pú for three years,
Kǒng Zǐ passed through it,
and upon entering the territory, praised him, saying:
"Yóu is respectful and trustworthy."
Entering the town, he said:
"Excellent!
"He uses zhōngxìn (忠信, loyalty and trustworthiness) to achieve kuān (寬, leniency)."
Upon reaching the court, he said:
"Excellent!
He uses míngchá (明察, clear discernment) to make duàn (斷, judgments)!"
Zǐgòng (子貢) held the reins and asked:
"Master, you have not seen Yóu (由) yet you praise him three times.
May I be permitted to hear why?"
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"Upon entering his territory,
the fields are very well-tended,
the weeds and wild growth are thoroughly cleared.
This is because he is respectful and trustworthy,
therefore the people exert their full effort.
Upon entering his city,
the walls and houses are very imposing,
the trees and vegetation are very luxuriant.
This is because he is loyal and trustworthy and achieves leniency,
so his people are not deceitful.
Upon entering his court,
it is very orderly.
This is because he uses clear discernment to make judgments,
therefore the people are not disruptive."
*Han Shi Wai Zhuan* (韓詩外傳) 8. Zǐ Jiàn (子賤) governed Dānfù (單父),
and his people were attached to him.
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"Tell Qiū (丘) how you govern."
He replied:
"I do not hesitate to open the granaries at the appropriate time,
to relieve the poor and destitute,
and to supplement those who are lacking."
Kǒngzǐ (孔子) said:
"This is merely attracting petty people;
it is not enough."
He replied:
"To reward the capable,
to recruit the virtuous,
and to dismiss the unworthy."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"This is a scholar's whispering in the ear,
not yet enough."
He replied:
"Those whom I treat as fathers are three,
those whom I treat as elder brothers are five,
those whom I treat as friends are twelve,
and my teacher is one person."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Those whom you treat as fathers are three,
those whom you treat as elder brothers are five,
that is enough to teach younger brothers;
those whom you treat as friends are twelve,
that is enough to dispel obstruction and concealment;
your teacher is one person,
that is enough to ensure that your deliberations are without missteps,
and that your actions are without failed achievements.
It is a pity that Bùqí is performing great deeds,
he is thus comparable to Yáo and Shùn."
《Shuō Yuàn·Zhèng Lǐ》 Confucius said to Mì Zǐjiàn:
"You govern Shànfù and are praised by the people.
Tell me how you do it." He replied:
"I treat fathers as fathers should be treated,
and sons as sons should be treated.
I care for the orphans and grieve at funerals."
Confucius said:
"Good,
these are small details,
and the common people will be attached to you,
but it is still not enough." He said:
"I, Bùqí, treat three people as fathers,
five people as elder brothers,
and eleven people as friends."
Confucius said:
"Treating three people as fathers can teach filial piety;
treating five people as elder brothers can teach brotherly love;
and befriending eleven people can teach learning.
This is a medium level,
and the middling people will be attached to you,
but it is still not enough." He said:
"In this area, there are five people more virtuous than I, Bùqí.
I serve them,
and they all teach me the techniques of governance."
Confucius said:
"If you desire the great,
then it lies in this.
In the past,
Yáo and Shùn purified and refined themselves,
in order to listen to and observe the world,
striving to attract worthy men.
Now, elevating worthy men
is the source of all blessings,
and the master of divine intelligence.
What is governed by the unrefined is small;
what is governed by the refined is great,
and such a person continues the work of Yáo and Shùn."
*Dà Dài Lǐ · Zǐ Zhāng Wèn Rù Guān* (The Elder Dai's Record of Rites · Zizhang Asks About Entering Office) Zǐ Zhāng asked Kǒngzǐ about entering officialdom.

if he walks these six paths,

Therefore, be discreet in your hearing.

*Dà Dài Lǐ·Qiān Shèng*. Gōng said:

teaching in its schools and communities,
